metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: or is it just a fundamentally flawed system?

body.input: Well, communism is like capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: The words mean many things to different people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: You could argue my life as a tenured professor

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: comes closer to communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: Anything the human race has seen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: and I would argue it works pretty well.

body.input: But look, if you mean the Soviet Union,

body.input: it devolved pretty quickly to a kind of decentralized

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: set of incentives that were destructive

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: rather than value maximizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: It wasn't even central planning, much less communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: So Paul Craig Roberts and Paul Ani were correct

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: in their descriptions of the Soviet system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: Think of it as weird mixes of barter

body.input: and malfunctioning incentives

body.input: and being very good at a whole bunch of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: But in terms of progress, innovation and consumer goods,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: it really being quite a failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: And now I wouldn't call that communism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: but that's what I think of the system the Soviets had.

body.input: And it required an ever increasing pile of lies

body.input: that by the end of the thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: And so it's, what is it, a momentum of bureaucracy

body.input: or something like that just builds up

body.input: or you lose control of the original vision

body.input: and practices and norms you had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: As you know, the Russian economy starting, what, 1999, 2000,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: has really quite a few years of super excellent growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: And Putin is still riding on that.

body.input: More or less coincides with his rise

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: as the truly focal figure on the scene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: Since then, pretty recently, they've had a bunch of years

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: of negative four to 5% growth in a row, which is terrible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: The economy is way too dependent on fossil fuels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: but the structural problem is this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: You need a concordance across economic power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: They don't have to be allocated identically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: but they have to be allocated consistently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: And the Russian system under Putin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: from almost the beginning, has never been able to have that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: that ultimately his incentives are to steer the system

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: where the economic power is in a small number of hands

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: in a non-diversified way.

body.input: The system won't deliver sustainable gains

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: in living standards anymore, ever, the way it's set up now,

body.input: that with fossil fuel prices go up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: they'll have some good years for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Tyler Cowen: Economic Growth & the Fight Against Conformity & Mediocrity | Lex Fridman Podcast #174

body.input: And that is really quite structural, what has gone wrong.

body.input: And then on top of that, you can have an opinion of Putin,

body.input: but you've got to start with those structural problems.

body.input: And that's why it's just not gonna work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Throughout history, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So the idea is that at the Big Bang,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: almost all the degrees of freedom that the universe could have

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: were there, but they were unentangled with anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And that's a reflection of the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that the Big Bang had a low entropy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It was a very simple, very small place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And as space expands, more and more degrees of freedom

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: become entangled with the rest of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Well, I have to ask John Carroll, what

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: do you think of the thought experiment from Nick Bostrom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that we're living in a simulation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So I think, let me contextualize that a little bit more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I think people don't actually take this thought experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I think it's quite interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It's not very useful, but it's quite interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: From the perspective of AI, a lot of the learning that can be done

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: usually happens in simulation, from artificial examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And so it's a constructive question to ask,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: how difficult is our real world to simulate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Which is kind of a dual part of if we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: living in a simulation and somebody built that simulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: if you were to try to do it yourself, how hard would it be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So obviously, we could be living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: If you just want the physical possibility,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: then I completely agree that it's physically possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I don't think that we actually are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So take this one piece of data into consideration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: We live in a big universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: There's two trillion galaxies in our observable universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: with 200 billion stars in each galaxy, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It would seem to be a waste of resources

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: to have a universe that big going on just

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: to do a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So in other words, I want to be a good Bayesian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I want to ask, under this hypothesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: what do I expect to see?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So the first thing I would say is, I wouldn't expect to see

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: a universe that was that big.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: OK?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: The second thing is, I wouldn't expect the resolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: of the universe to be as good as it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So it's always possible that if there are superhuman simulators

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: only have finite resources, that they don't render

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: the entire universe, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That the part that is out there, the two trillion galaxies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: isn't actually being simulated fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But then the obvious extrapolation of that

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: is that only I am being simulated fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: The rest of you are just non-player characters, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I'm the only thing that is real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: The rest of you are just chatbots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Beyond this wall, I see the wall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But there is literally nothing on the other side of the wall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That is sort of the Bayesian prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That's what it would be like to do an efficient simulation of me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So none of that seems quite realistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I don't see, I hear the argument that it's just possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: and easy to simulate lots of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I don't see any evidence from what

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: we know about our universe that we look like a simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Now, maybe you could say, well, we don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: know what it would look like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But that's just abandoning your Bayesian responsibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Your job is to say, under this theory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: here's what you would expect to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Yeah, so certainly if you think about simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: as a thing that's like a video game where only a small subset

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: is being rendered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But say, all the laws of physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: the entire closed system of the quote, unquote, universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: it had a creator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Yeah, it's always possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Right, so that's not useful to think about when

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: you're thinking about physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: The way Nick Bostrom phrases it, if it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: possible to simulate a universe, eventually we'll do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: You can use that, by the way, for a lot of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Well, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But I guess the question is, how hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: is it to create a universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I wrote a little blog post about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And maybe I'm missing something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But there's an argument that says not only

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that it might be possible to simulate a universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: but probably if you imagine that you actually attribute

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: consciousness and agency to the little things that we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: simulating, to our little artificial beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: there's probably a lot more of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: than there are ordinary organic beings in the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: or there will be in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So there's an argument that not only is being a simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: possible, it's probable because in the space of all living

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: consciousnesses, most of them are being simulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Most of them are not at the top level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I think that argument must be wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: because it follows from that argument that if we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: simulated, but we can also simulate other things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: but if we can simulate other things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: they can simulate other things if we give them

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: enough power and resolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And ultimately, we'll reach a bottom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: because the laws of physics in our universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: have a bottom made of atoms and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So there will be the cheapest possible simulations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And if you believe the original argument,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: you should conclude that we should

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: be in the cheapest possible simulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: because that's where most people are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: But we don't look like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It doesn't look at all like we're at the edge of resolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that we're 16-bit things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It seems much easier to make much lower level things

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: than we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And also, I question the whole approach

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: to the anthropic principle that says we are typical observers

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I think that that's not actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: I think that there's a lot of selection

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that we can do that we're typical within things we already

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: know, but not typical within all of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So do you think there is intelligent life, however

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: you would like to define intelligent life, out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: in the universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: My guess is that there is not intelligent life

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: in the observable universe other than us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: simply on the basis of the fact that the likely number

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: of other intelligent species in the observable universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: there's two likely numbers, zero or billions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And if there had been billions, you would have noticed already.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: For there to be literally a small number, like Star Trek,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: there's a dozen intelligent civilizations in our galaxy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: but not a billion, that's weird.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That's sort of bizarre to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It's easy for me to imagine that there are zero others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: because there's just a big bottleneck

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: to making multicellular life or technological life

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: It's very hard for me to imagine that there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: a whole bunch out there that have somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: been hidden from us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: The question I'd like to ask is, what would intelligent life

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: What I mean by that question and where it's going

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: is, what if intelligent life is just

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: in some very big ways different than the one that

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: has on Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That there's all kinds of intelligent life

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: that operates at different scales of both size

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: and temporal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That's a great possibility, because I

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: think we should be humble about what intelligence is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: what life is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: We don't even agree on what life is, much less

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: what intelligent life is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So that's an argument for humility,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: saying there could be intelligent life

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: of a very different character.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: You could imagine the dolphins are intelligent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: but never invent space travel, because they live in the ocean

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: and they don't have thumbs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: So they never invent technology, they never invent smelting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Maybe the universe is full of intelligent species that just

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: don't make technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: That's compatible with the data, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: And I think maybe what you're pointing at

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: is even more out there versions of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: Intelligence in intermolecular clouds

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

metadata.title: Podcast: Sean Carroll: The Nature of the Universe, Life, and Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #26

body.input: He's truly an out-of-the-box thinker and a fun personality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I really enjoy talking to him.
