body.input: Also, Twitter, LinkedIn, aji.mit.edu if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: want to watch other lectures or conversations like this one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Better yet, go read Max's book, Life 3.0, Chapter 7 on Goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is my favorite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's really where philosophy and engineering come together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And it opens with a quote by Dostoevsky,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the mystery of human existence lies not in just staying alive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but in finding something to live for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Lastly, I believe that every failure rewards us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with an opportunity to learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In that sense, I've been very fortunate to fail

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in so many new and exciting ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And this conversation was no different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I've learned about something called radio frequency

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: interference, RFI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Look it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Apparently, music and conversations

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: from local radio stations can bleed into the audio

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that you're recording in such a way that almost completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: ruins that audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's an exceptionally difficult sound source to remove.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I've gotten the opportunity to learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: how to avoid RFI in the future during recording sessions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I've also gotten the opportunity to learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: how to use Adobe Audition and iZotope RX 6

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to do some noise, some audio repair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Of course, this is an exceptionally difficult noise

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to remove.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I am an engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm not an audio engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Neither is anybody else in our group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But we did our best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Nevertheless, I thank you for your patience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I hope you're still able to enjoy this conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Do you think there's intelligent life out there in the universe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let's open up with an easy question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I have a minority of you here, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: When I give public lectures, I often

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: ask for a show of hands who thinks

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: there is intelligent life out there somewhere else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And almost everyone put their hands up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And when I ask why, they'll be like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: oh, there's so many galaxies out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's got to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But I'm a numbers nerd, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So when you look more carefully at it, it's not so clear at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: When we talk about our universe, first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we don't mean all of space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: We actually mean, I don't know, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: can throw me the universe if you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's behind you there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: We simply mean the spherical region of space

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: from which light has had time to reach us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so far during the 14.8 billion years, 13.8 billion years

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: since our big bang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's more space here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But this is what we call a universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because that's all we have access to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So is there intelligent life here

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that's gotten to the point of building telescopes

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and computers?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: My guess is no, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The probability of it happening on any given planet

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is some number we don't know what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And what we do know is that the number can't be super high,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because there's over a billion Earth-like planets in the Milky

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Way galaxy alone, many of which are billions of years older

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And aside from some UFO believers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: there isn't much evidence that any super-dense civilization

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: has come here at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And so that's the famous Fermi paradox, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then if you work the numbers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what you find is that if you have no clue what

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the probability is of getting life on a given planet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so it could be 10 to the minus 10, 10 to the minus 20,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or 10 to the minus 2, any power of 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is sort of equally likely if you want to be really open-minded.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That translates into it being equally likely

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that our nearest neighbor is 10 to the 16 meters away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: 10 to the 17 meters away, 10 to the 18.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: By the time you get much less than 10 to the 16 already,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: pretty much know there is nothing else that close.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And when you get beyond 10.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because they would have discovered us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, they would have discovered us long ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or if they're really close, we would have probably

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: noted some engineering projects that they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And if it's beyond 10 to the 26 meters,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that's already outside of here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So my guess is actually that we are the only life in here

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that's gotten to the point of building advanced tech, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think puts a lot of responsibility on our shoulders

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to not screw up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think people who take for granted

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that it's OK for us to screw up, have an accidental nuclear war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: go extinct somehow because there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a sort of Star Trek-like situation out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: where some other life forms are going to come and bail us out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And it doesn't matter as much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think alliling us into a false sense of security.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think it's much more prudent to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: let's be really grateful for this amazing opportunity

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we've had and make the best of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just in case it is down to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So from a physics perspective, do you think intelligent life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so it's unique from a sort of statistical view

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the size of the universe, but from the basic matter

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the universe, how difficult is it for intelligent life

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to come about, the kind of advanced tech building life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Is implied in your statement that it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: really difficult to create something like a human species?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Well, I think what we know is that going from no life

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to having life that can do a level of tech,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: there is some sort of two going beyond that

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than actually settling our whole universe with life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There is some major roadblock there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which is some great filter as it's sometimes called,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which is tough to get through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's either that roadblock is either behind us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or in front of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm hoping very much that it's behind us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm super excited every time we get a new report from NASA

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: saying they failed to find any life on Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Like, yes, awesome, because that suggests that the hard part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: maybe it was getting the first ribosome

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or some very low level kind of stepping stone

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so that we're home free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because if that's true, then the future

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is really only limited by our own imagination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It would be much suckier if it turns out

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that this level of life is kind of a diamond dozen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But maybe there is some other problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Like, as soon as a civilization gets advanced technology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: within 100 years, they get into some stupid fight

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with themselves and poof.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That would be a bummer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, so you've explored the mysteries

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the cosmological universe, the one that's between us today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think you've also begun to explore the other universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which is sort of the mystery, the mysterious universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the mind, of intelligence, of intelligent life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So is there a common thread between your interest

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and the way you think about space and intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Oh, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: When I was a teenager, I was already very fascinated

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by the biggest questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I felt that the two biggest mysteries of all in science

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: were our universe out there and our universe in here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it's quite natural, after having

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: spent a quarter of a century on my career thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a lot about this one, that I'm now

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: indulging in the luxury of doing research on this one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's just so cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I feel the time is ripe now for you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: transdrakely deepening our understanding of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Just start exploring this one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, because I think a lot of people view intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as something mysterious that can only exist

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in biological organisms like us, and therefore dismiss

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: all talk about artificial general intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as science fiction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But from my perspective as a physicist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I am a blob of quarks and electrons

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: moving around in a certain pattern

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and processing information in certain ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And this is also a blob of quarks and electrons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm not smarter than the water bottle

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because I'm made of different kind of quarks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm made of up quarks and down quarks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: exact same kind as this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's no secret sauce, I think, in me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's all about the pattern of the information processing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And this means that there's no law of physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: saying that we can't create technology, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: can help us by being incredibly intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and help us crack mysteries that we couldn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In other words, I think we've really only seen the tip

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the intelligence iceberg so far.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, so the perceptronium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So you coined this amazing term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's a hypothetical state of matter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: sort of thinking from a physics perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what is the kind of matter that can help, as you're saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: subjective experience emerge, consciousness emerge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So how do you think about consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: from this physics perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So again, I think many people have underestimated

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: our ability to make progress on this

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by convincing themselves it's hopeless because somehow we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: missing some ingredient that we need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's some new consciousness particle or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I happen to think that we're not missing anything

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and that it's not the interesting thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about consciousness that gives us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: this amazing subjective experience of colors and sounds

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and emotions and so on is rather something at the higher level

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about the patterns of information processing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And that's why I like to think about this idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of perceptronium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: What does it mean for an arbitrary physical system

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to be conscious in terms of what its particles are doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or its information is doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think, I hate carbon chauvinism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: this attitude you have to be made of carbon atoms

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to be smart or conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So something about the information processing

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that this kind of matter performs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, and you can see I have my favorite equations here

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: describing various fundamental aspects of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I feel that I think one day maybe someone who's watching

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: this will come up with the equations that information

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: processing has to satisfy to be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm quite convinced there is big discovery to be made there

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because let's face it, we know that some information

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: processing is conscious because we are conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But we also know that a lot of information processing

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is not conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Like most of the information processing happening

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in your brain right now is not conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There are like 10 megabytes per second coming in

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: even just through your visual system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're not conscious about your heartbeat

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or your blood pressure or your blood pressure

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or your blood pressure regulation or most things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Even if I just ask you to read what it says here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: you look at it and then, oh, now you know what it said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're not aware of how the computation actually happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're like, your consciousness is like the CEO

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that got an email at the end with the final answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So what is it that makes a difference?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think that's both of those great science mystery,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we're actually studying it a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but it's just a really urgent question to answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: For starters, I mean, if you're an emergency room doctor

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and you have an unresponsive patient coming in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: wouldn't it be great if in addition to having

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a CT scanner, you had a consciousness scanner

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that could figure out whether this person

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is actually having locked in syndrome

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or is actually comatose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And in the future, imagine if we build robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or the machine that we can have really good conversations

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with, I think is most likely to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Wouldn't you wanna know if your home helper robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is actually experiencing anything or just like a zombie?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Would you prefer it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: What would you prefer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Would you prefer that it's actually unconscious

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so that you don't have to feel guilty

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about switching it off or giving boring chores?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or what would you prefer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Well, certainly I would prefer

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the appearance of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But the question is whether the appearance of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is different than consciousness itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And sort of to ask that as a question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: do you think we need to understand what consciousness is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: solve the hard problem of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in order to build something like an AGI system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: No, I don't think that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I think we will probably be able to build things

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: even if we don't answer that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But if we wanna make sure that what happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is a good thing, we better solve it first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it's a wonderful controversy you're raising there

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: where you have basically three points of view

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about the hard problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there are two different points of view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They both conclude that the hard problem of consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is BS.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: On one hand, you have some people like Daniel Dennett

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: who say this is consciousness is just BS

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because consciousness is the same thing as intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's no difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So anything which acts conscious is conscious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just like we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then there are also a lot of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: including many top AI researchers I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: who say, oh, consciousness is just bullshit

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because of course machines can never be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They're always gonna be zombies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You never have to feel guilty about how you treat them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then there's a third group of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: including Giulio Tononi, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and another, and Christoph Koch and her brothers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I would put myself also in this middle camp

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: who say that actually some information processing

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is conscious and some is not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So let's find the equation

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which can be used to determine which it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I think we've just been a little bit lazy

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: kind of running away from this problem for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's been almost taboo even mentioned the C word

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in a lot of circles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because, but we should stop making excuses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: This is a science question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And there are ways we can even test any theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that makes predictions for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And coming back to this helper robot, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so you said you would want your helper robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to certainly act conscious and treat you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: like you have conversations with you and stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But wouldn't you feel a little bit creeped out

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: if you realized that it was just like lost up tape recorder

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that was just zombie and was a faking emotion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Would you prefer that it actually had an experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or would you prefer that it's actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: not experiencing anything so you don't have to feel guilty

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about what you do to it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's such a difficult question because,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's like when you're in a relationship and you say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: well, I love you and the other person said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I love you back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's like asking, well, do they really love you back

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or are they just saying they love you back?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Don't you really want them to actually love you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's hard to really know the difference between

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: everything seeming like there's consciousness present,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: there's intelligence present,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: there's affection, passion, love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and it actually being there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm not sure, do you have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But like, can I ask you a question about this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: To make it a bit more pointed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So Mass General Hospital is right across the river, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Suppose you're going in for a medical procedure

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and they're like, for anesthesia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what we're gonna do is we're gonna give you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a muscle relaxant so you won't be able to move

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and you're gonna feel excruciating pain

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: during the whole surgery

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but you won't be able to do anything about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But then we're gonna give you this drug

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that erases your memory of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Would you be cool about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: What's the difference that you're conscious about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or not if there's no behavioral change, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right, that's a really clear way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, it feels like in that sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: experiencing it is a valuable quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So actually being able to have subjective experiences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: at least in that case, is valuable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I think we humans have a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of a bad track record also

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of making these self-serving arguments

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that other entities aren't conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: People often say, oh, these animals can't feel pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's okay to boil lobsters because we asked them

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: if it hurt and they didn't say anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And now there was just a paper out saying lobsters

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: did do feel pain when you boil them

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and they're banning it in Switzerland.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And we did this with slaves too often

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and said, oh, they don't mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They don't maybe aren't conscious

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or women don't have souls or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I'm a little bit nervous when I hear people

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just take as an axiom that machines

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: can't have experience ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think this is just a really fascinating science question

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let's research it and try to figure out what it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that makes the difference between unconscious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: intelligent behavior and conscious, intelligent behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So in terms of, so if you think of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Boston Dynamics humanoid robot being sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with a broom being pushed around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it starts pushing on its consciousness question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So let me ask, do you think an AGI system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: like a few neuroscientists believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: needs to have a physical embodiment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It needs to have a body or something like a body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: No, I don't think so.

body.input: You mean to have a conscious experience?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: To have consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I do think it helps a lot to have a physical embodiment

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to learn the kind of things about the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that are important to us humans for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But I don't think the physical embodiment

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is necessary after you've learned it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just have the experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Think about when you're dreaming, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Your eyes are closed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're not getting any sensory input.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're not behaving or moving in any way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but there's still an experience there, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And so clearly the experience that you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: when you see something cool in your dreams

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: isn't coming from your eyes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's just the information processing itself in your brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which is that experience, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But if I put it another way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'll say because it comes from neuroscience

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is the reason you wanna have a body and a physical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: something like a physical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a physical system is because you want to be able

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to preserve something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In order to have a self, you could argue,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: you'd need to have some kind of embodiment of self

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to want to preserve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Well, now we're getting a little bit anthropomorphic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Anthropomorphizing things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: maybe talking about self-preservation instincts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I mean, we are evolved organisms, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So Darwinian evolution endowed us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and other evolved organism with a self-preservation instinct

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because those that didn't have those self-preservation genes

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: got cleaned out of the gene pool, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But if you build an artificial general intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the mind space that you can design is much, much larger

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than just a specific subset of minds that can evolve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So an AGI mind doesn't necessarily have

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to have any self-preservation instinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It also doesn't necessarily have to be so individualistic

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as us, like imagine if you could just,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: first of all, or we're also very afraid of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Suppose you could back yourself up every five minutes

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and then your airplane is about to crash.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You're like, shucks, I'm gonna lose the last five minutes

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of experiences since my last cloud backup, bang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's not as big a deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or if we could just copy experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: between our minds easily, which we could easily do

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: if we were silicon-based, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Then maybe we would feel a little bit more

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: like a hive mind actually, maybe it's the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I don't think we should take for granted at all

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that AGI will have to have any of those sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: competitive as alpha male instincts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And this is really interesting because I think some people

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: go too far and say, of course, we don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to have any concerns either that advanced AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: will have those instincts because we can build anything

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we want, that there's a very nice set of arguments

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: going back to Steve Omohundro and Nick Bostrom and others

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just pointing out that when we build machines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we normally build them with some kind of goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: win this chess game, drive this car safely

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And as soon as you put in a goal into machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: especially if it's kind of open-ended goal

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and the machine is very intelligent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it'll break that down into a bunch of sub goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And one of those goals will almost always

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: be self-preservation because if it breaks or dies

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in the process, it's not gonna accomplish the goal, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Like suppose you just build a little,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: you have a little robot and you tell it to go down

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to star market here and get you some food,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: make you cook you an Italian dinner, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and then someone mugs it and tries to break it on the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That robot has an incentive to not get destroyed

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and defend itself for runaway because otherwise

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's gonna fail in cooking you dinner.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's not afraid of death, but it really wants to

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: complete the dinner cooking goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it will have a self-preservation instinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Continue being a functional agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And similarly, if you give any kind of more

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: ambitious goal to an AGI, it's very likely to wanna

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: acquire more resources so it can do that better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And it's exactly from those sort of sub goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that we might not have intended that some of the concerns

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about AGI safety come.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You give it some goal that seems completely harmless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then before you realize it, it's also trying to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: these other things which you didn't want it to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and it's maybe smarter than us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So, so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let me pause just because I am in a very kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: human centric way, see fear of death as a valuable motivator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So you don't think, you think that's an artifact

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of evolution, so that's the kind of mind space

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: evolution created that we're sort of almost obsessed

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about self-preservation, some kind of genetic well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You don't think that's necessary to be afraid of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So not just a kind of sub goal of self-preservation

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just so you can keep doing the thing, but more

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: fundamentally sort of have the finite thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: like this ends for you at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Do I think it's necessary for what precisely?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: For intelligence, but also for consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So for those, for both, do you think really

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: like a finite death and the fear of it is important?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So before I can answer, before we can agree on whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's necessary for intelligence or for consciousness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we should be clear on how we define those two words

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because a lot of really smart people define them

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in very different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I was in this, on this panel with AI experts

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and they couldn't agree on how to define intelligence even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I define intelligence simply as the ability

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to accomplish complex goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I like your broad definition because again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't wanna be a carbon chauvinist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And in that case, no, certainly it doesn't require

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: fear of death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I would say alpha go, alpha zero is quite intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think alpha zero has any fear of being turned off

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because it doesn't understand the concept of it even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And similarly, consciousness, I mean, you can certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: imagine very simple kind of experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: If certain plants have any kind of experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think they're very afraid of dying

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or there's nothing they can do about it anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there wasn't much value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But more seriously, I think if you ask not just

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: about being conscious, but maybe having

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what we might call an exciting life

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: where you feel passion and really appreciate

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the things, maybe there perhaps it does help

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: having a backdrop that, hey, it's finite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let's make the most of this, let's live to the fullest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So if you knew you were gonna just live forever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: do you think you would change your?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, I mean, in some perspective, it would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: an incredibly boring life living forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So in the sort of loose subjective terms that you said

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of something exciting and something in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that other humans would understand, I think, is yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it seems that the finiteness of it is important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Well, the good news I have for you then is

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: based on what we understand about cosmology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: everything in our universe is ultimately probably finite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Big crunch or big, what's the infinite expansion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, we could have a big chill or a big crunch

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or a big rip or the big snap or death bubbles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: All of them are more than a billion years away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So we certainly have vastly more time

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than our ancestors thought, but there is still

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: pretty hard to squeeze in an infinite number

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of compute cycles, even though there are some loopholes

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that just might be possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But I think some people like to say that you should live

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as if you're gonna die in five years or so,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and that's sort of optimal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Maybe it's a good assumption, we should build

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: our civilization as if it's all finite

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to be on the safe side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So you mentioned defining intelligence as

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the ability to solve complex goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Where would you draw a line?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: How would you try to define human level intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and superhuman level intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Where is consciousness part of that definition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: No, consciousness does not come into this definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I think of intelligence as a spectrum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but there are very many different kinds of goals you can have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You can have a goal to be a good chess player,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a good go player, a good car driver,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a good investor, good poet, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So intelligence by its very nature

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: isn't something you can measure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but it's one number, some overall goodness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: No, no, there are some people who are better at this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: some people are better at that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right now we have machines that are much better than us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: at some very narrow tasks, like multiplying large numbers fast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: memorizing large databases, playing chess,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: playing Go, and soon driving cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But there's still no machine that can match a human child

body.input: in general intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But artificial general intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: AGI, the name of your course, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that is by its very definition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as well as we can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1
