metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in the 60s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: If that ever happens, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think it's going to be the biggest transition

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in the history of life on earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But it doesn't necessarily have to wait the big impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: until machines are better than us at knitting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The really big change doesn't come exactly at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They're better than us at everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The really big change comes first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Their big change is when they start becoming better at us

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: at doing most of the jobs that we do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because that takes away much of the demand for human labor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then the really whopping change

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: comes when they become better than us at AI research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because right now, the time scale of AI research

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is limited by the human research and development cycle of years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: typically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: How long does it take from one release of some software

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or iPhone or whatever to the next?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But once Google can replace 40,000 engineers

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by 40,000 equivalent pieces of software or whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: then there's no reason that has to be years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It can be, in principle, much faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And the time scale of future progress in AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and all of science and technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: will be driven by machines, not humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it's this simple point which gives right

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to this incredibly fun controversy about whether there

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: can be intelligence explosion, so-called singularity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as Werner Wienz called it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The idea, as articulated by I.J. Good,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: is obviously way back in the 50s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But you can see Alan Turing and others thought about it

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: even earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You asked me what exactly would I define human level at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So the glib answer is to say something

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which is better than us at all cognitive tasks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or better than any human at all cognitive tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But the really interesting bar, I

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: think, goes a little bit lower than that, actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's when they're better than us at AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: programming and general learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: so that they can, if they want to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: get better than us at anything by just studying up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there, better is a key word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And better is towards this spectrum

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of the complexity of goals it's able to accomplish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So another way to, and that's certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a very clear definition of human level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it's almost like a sea that's rising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You can do more and more and more things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's actually a graphic that you show.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's a really nice way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there's some peaks, and there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: an ocean level elevating, and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: solve more and more problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But just to take a pause, and we took a bunch of questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and a lot of social networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And a bunch of people asked a slightly different direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: on creativity, on things that perhaps aren't a peak.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Human beings are flawed, and perhaps better

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: means having contradiction, being flawed in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So let me sort of start easy, first of all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So you have a lot of cool equations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let me ask, what's your favorite equation, first of all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I know they're all like your children, but which one is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: This is the Schrodinger equation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's the master key of quantum mechanics of the micro world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So with this equation, we can calculate everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to do with atoms, molecules, and all the way up to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, so quantum mechanics is certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a beautiful, mysterious formulation of our world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I'd like to ask you, just as an example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it perhaps doesn't have the same beauty as physics does,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but in mathematics, abstract, the Andrew Wiles, who

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: proved the Fermat's last theorem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I just saw this recently, and it

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: kind of caught my eye a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: This is 358 years after it was conjectured.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So this very simple formulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Everybody tried to prove it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Everybody failed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And so here's this guy comes along, and eventually proves it

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and then fails to prove it and then proves it again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In 94, and he said the moment when everything connected

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: into place, in an interview he said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it was so indescribably beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That moment when you finally realized

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the connecting piece of two conjectures, he said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it was so indescribably beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It was so simple and so elegant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I couldn't understand how I'd missed it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and I just stared at it in disbelief for 20 minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Then during the day, I walked around the department,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and I'd keep coming back to my desk,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: looking to see if it was still there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It was still there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I couldn't contain myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I was so excited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It was the most important moment of my working life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Nothing I ever do again will mean as much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So that particular moment, and it kind of made me think of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what would it take?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I think we have all been there at small levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Maybe you let me ask, have you had a moment like that

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in your life where you just had an idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's like, wow, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I wouldn't mention myself in the same breath as Andrew Wiles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but I've certainly had a number of aha moments

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: when I realized something very cool about physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: just completely made my head explode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In fact, some of my favorite discoveries I made,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I later realized that they had been discovered earlier

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by someone who sometimes got quite famous for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So it's too late for me to even publish it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: but that doesn't diminish in any way

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the emotional experience you have when you realize it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Like, wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, so what would it take in that moment, that wow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that was yours in that moment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So what do you think it takes for an intelligent system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: an AGI system, an AI system to have a moment like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That's a tricky question

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because there are actually two parts to it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: One of them is, can it accomplish that proof?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Can it prove that you can never write

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: A to the N plus B to the N equals three to that equals Z to the N

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: for all integers, et cetera, et cetera,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: when one end is bigger than two?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That's simply a question about intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Can you build machines that are that intelligent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I think by the time we get a machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that can independently come up with that level of proofs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: probably quite close to AGI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The second question is a question about consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: When will we, how likely is it that such a machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: would actually have any experience at all

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as opposed to just being like a zombie?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And would we expect it to have some sort of emotional response

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: to this or anything at all akin to human emotion

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: where when it accomplishes its machine goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it reviews it as somehow something very positive

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and sublime and deeply meaningful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I would certainly hope that if in the future

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we do create machines that are our peers

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: or even our descendants,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that I would certainly hope that they do have

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: this sort of sublime appreciation of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In a way, my absolutely worst nightmare would be that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: at some point in the future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the distant future maybe our cosmos is teeming

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with all this post-biological life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: doing all the seemingly cool stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And maybe the last humans by the time our species eventually

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: fizzles out will be like, well, that's okay,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: because we're so proud of our descendants here

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and look at what all the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: My worst nightmare is that we haven't solved

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the consciousness problem and we haven't realized

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that these are all the zombies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They're not aware of anything any more than a tape recorder

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as an any kind of experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So the whole thing has just become a play for empty benches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That would be like the ultimate zombie apocalypse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So I would much rather in that case that we have these beings

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: which can really appreciate how amazing it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And in that picture, what would be the role of creativity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: A few people ask about creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Do you think, when you think about intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I mean, certainly the story you told at the beginning

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: of your book involved creating movies and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Sort of making money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You can make a lot of money in our modern world

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with music and movies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So if you are an intelligent system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: you may want to get good at that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But that's not necessarily what I mean by creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Is it important on that complex goals where the sea is rising

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: for there to be something creative?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or am I being very human-centric

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and thinking creativity is somehow special

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: relative to intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: My hunch is that we should think of creativity

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: simply as an aspect of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And we have to be very careful with human vanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: We have this tendency to very often want to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: as soon as machines can do something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we try to diminish it and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: oh, but that's not like real intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because they're not creative or this or that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The other thing, if we ask ourselves to write down

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: a definition of what we actually mean

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by being creative, what we mean by Andrew Wiles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what he did there, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: don't we often mean that someone takes a very unexpected leap?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Mm-hmm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's not like taking 573 and multiplying it by 224

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: by just a step of straightforward cookbook-like rules, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You can maybe make a connection between two things

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that people have never thought was connected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's very surprising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think this is an aspect of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And this is actually one of the most important aspects of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Maybe the reason we humans tend to be better at it

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than traditional computers is because

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's something that comes more naturally

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: if you're a neural network

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: than if you're a traditional logic gate-based computer machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: We physically have all these connections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And if you activate here, activate here, activate here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's ping!

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You know, my hunch is that if we ever build a machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: where you could just give it the task,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: hey, hey, you say, hey, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I just realized I want to travel around the world instead this month.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Can you teach my AGI course for me?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And it's like, OK, I'll do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'll do the other thing that you would have done,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and the improvisers and stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That would, in my mind, involve a lot of creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, so it's actually a beautiful way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think we do try to grasp at the, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: the definition of intelligence is everything we don't understand how to build.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So we as humans try to find things that we have and machines don't have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Maybe creativity is just one of the things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: one of the words we use to describe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That's a really interesting way to put it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think we need to be that defensive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think anything good comes out of saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: oh, we're somehow special, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's, contrary-wise, there are many examples in history of where

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: trying to pretend that we're somehow superior to all other intelligent beings

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: led to pretty bad results, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: In Nazi Germany, they said that they were somehow superior to other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Today, we still do a lot of cruelty to animals by saying that we're so superior somehow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and they can't feel pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Slavery was justified by the same kind of really weak arguments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think if we actually go ahead and build artificial general intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we can do things better than us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think we should try to found our self-worth on some sort of bogus claims of superiority

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: in terms of our intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think we should instead find our calling and the meaning of life from the experiences that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I can have very meaningful experiences, even if there are other people who are smarter than me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: When I go to a faculty meeting here, and we're talking about something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and I suddenly realize, oh, he has an old prize, he has an old prize, he has an old prize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Does that make me enjoy life any less or enjoy talking to those people less?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Of course not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Contrary, I feel very honored and privileged to get to interact with other very intelligent beings

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that are better than me at a lot of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I don't think there's any reason why we can't have the same approach with intelligent machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That's a really interesting...

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: People don't often think about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They think about if there's machines that are more intelligent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: you naturally think that that's not going to be a beneficial type of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You don't realize it could be peers with Nobel prizes that would be just fun to talk with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They might be clever about certain topics, and you can have fun having a few drinks with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Also, another example we can all relate to of why it doesn't have to be a terrible thing to be impressed

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: with people who are even smarter than us all around is when you and I were both two years old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Our parents were much more intelligent than us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It worked out okay because their goals were aligned with our goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That, I think, is really the number one key issue we have to solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The value alignment problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: People who see too many Hollywood movies with lousy science fiction plot lines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: they worry about the wrong thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They worry about some machine suddenly turning evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's not malice that's the issue, the concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's competence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: By definition, intelligence makes you very competent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: If you have a more intelligent go-playing computer, playing as a less intelligent one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and when we define intelligence as the ability to accomplish go-winning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: it's going to be the more intelligent one that wins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: If you have a human and then you have an AGI that's more intelligent in all ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and they have different goals, guess who's going to get their way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I was just reading about this particular rhinoceros species that was driven extinct just a few years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It was a bummer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I was looking at this cute picture of a mommy rhinoceros with its child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Why did we humans drive it to extinction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It wasn't because we were evil rhino haters as a whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It was just because our goals weren't aligned with those of the rhinoceros,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: and it didn't work out so well for the rhinoceros because we were more intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think it's just so important that if we ever do build AGI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: before we unleash anything, we have to make sure that it learns to understand our goals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: that it adopts our goals, and it retains those goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So the cool, interesting problem there is us as human beings trying to formulate our values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: You could think of the United States Constitution as a way that people sat down,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: at the time a bunch of white men, which is a good example, we should say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: They formulated the goals for this country, and a lot of people agree that those goals actually held up pretty well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's an interesting formulation of values and failed miserably in other ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So for the value alignment problem and the solution to it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: we have to be able to put on paper or in a program human values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: How difficult do you think that is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Very. But it's so important. We really have to give it our best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And it's difficult for two separate reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's the technical value alignment problem of figuring out how to make machines understand our goals, adopt them, and retain them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then there's the separate part of it, the philosophical part, whose values anyway?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And since it's not like we have any great consensus on this planet on values,

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: what mechanism should we create then to aggregate and decide, OK, what's a good compromise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That second discussion can't just be left the tech nerds like myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: That's right. And if we refuse to talk about it and then AGI gets built, who's going to be actually making the decision about whose values?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: It's going to be a bunch of dudes and some tech company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And are they necessarily so representative of all of humankind that we want to just entrust it to them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Are they even uniquely qualified to speak to future human happiness just because they're good at programming AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'd much rather have this be a really inclusive conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But do you think it's possible sort of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So you create a beautiful vision that includes sort of the diversity, cultural diversity and various perspectives on discussing rights, freedoms, human dignity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But how hard is it to come to that consensus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Do you think it's certainly a really important thing that we should all try to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But do you think it's feasible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I think there's no better way to guarantee failure than to refuse to talk about it or refuse to try.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And I also think it's a really bad strategy to say, OK, let's first have a discussion for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then once we reach complete consensus, then we'll try to load it into some machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: No, we shouldn't let perfect be the enemy of good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Instead, we should start with the kindergarten ethics that pretty much everybody agrees on and put that into machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Now, we're not doing that even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Look at anyone who builds a passenger aircraft wants to never under any circumstances fly into a building or mountain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Right. Yet the September 11 hijackers were able to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And even more embarrassingly, you know, and the gas lube, it's this depressed German wings pilot when he flew his passenger jet into the Alps, killing over 100 people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: He just told the autopilot to do it. He told the freeing computer to change the altitude to 100 meters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And even though it had the GPS maps, everything the computer was like, OK, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So we we should take those very basic values where the problem is not that we don't agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: The problem is just we've been too lazy to try to put it into our machines and make sure that from now on, airplanes will just which all have computers in them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: We just never just refuse to do something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Go into safe mode, maybe lock the cockpit door, go to the nearest airport.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And and there's so much other technology in our world as well now where it's really quite becoming quite timely to put in some sort of very basic values like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Even in cars, we have had enough vehicle terrorism attacks by now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: If you have driven trucks and vans into pedestrians, that is not at all a crazy idea to just have that hardwired into the car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Because, yeah, there are a lot of there's always going to be people who for some reason want to harm others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: But most of those people don't have the technical expertise to figure out how to work around something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So if the car just won't do it. It helps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So let's start there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there's a lot of that's a that's a great point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So not not chasing perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: There's a lot of things that a lot that most of the world agrees on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Yeah, and start there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Let's start there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And then once we start there, we'll also get into the habit of having these kind of conversations about, OK, what else should we put in here and have these discussions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: This should be a gradual process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Great. So but that also means describing these things and describing it to a machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So one thing we had a few conversations with Stephen Wolfram.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I'm not sure if you're familiar with Stephen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Oh, yeah, I know him quite well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So he is, you know, he play, you know, works with a bunch of things, but, you know, cellular automata, the simple, computable things, these computation systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And you kind of mentioned that, you know, we probably have already within these systems already something that's a GI, meaning like we just don't know it because we can't talk to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So if you give me this chance to try to at least form a question out of this is I think it's an interesting idea to think that we can have intelligent systems, but we don't know how to describe something to them and they can't communicate with us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: I know you're doing a little bit of work and explainable I trying to get a to explain itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So what are your thoughts of natural language processing or some kind of other communication?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: How how does the AI explain something to us?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: How do we explain something to it to machines?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: Or you think of it differently?

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: So there are two separate parts to your question there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: One of them has to do with communication, which is super interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Max Tegmark: Life 3.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #1

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Francois Chalet.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: What philosophers, thinkers or ideas had a big impact

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: on you growing up and today?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So one author that had a big impact on me

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: when I read his books as a teenager

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: was Jean Piaget, who is a Swiss psychologist,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: is considered to be the father of developmental psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and he has a large body of work about basically

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: how intelligence develops in children.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And so it's really old work,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: like most of it is from the 1930s, 1940s.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So it's not quite up to date.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: It's actually superseded by many newer developments

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in developmental psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: But to me, it was very interesting, very striking

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and actually shaped the early ways in which I started

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: thinking about the mind and development of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: as a teenager.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: His actual ideas or the way he thought about it

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: or just the fact that you could think about

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: the developing mind at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: I guess both.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Jean Piaget is the author that really introduced me

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to the notion that intelligence and the mind

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: is something that you construct throughout your life

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and that children construct it in stages.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And I thought that was a very interesting idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: which is, of course, very relevant to AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to building artificial minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Another book that I read around the same time

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that had a big impact on me,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and there was actually a little bit of overlap

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: with Jean Piaget as well,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and I read it around the same time,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: is Jeff Harkin's, On Intelligence, which is a classic.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And he has this vision of the mind as a multi-scale hierarchy

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: of temporal prediction modules.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And these ideas really resonated with me,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: like the notion of a modular hierarchy

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: of potentially compression functions

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: or prediction functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: I thought it was really, really interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And it really shaped the way I started thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: about how to build minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: The hierarchical nature, which aspect.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Also, he's a neuroscientist, so he was thinking actual,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: he was basically talking about how our mind works.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yeah, the notion that cognition is prediction

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: was an idea that was kind of new to me at the time

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and that I really loved at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And yeah, and the notion that there are multiple scales

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: of processing in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: The hierarchy.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: This was before deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: These ideas of hierarchies,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in here I've been around for a long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: even before On Intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: they've been around since the 1980s.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And yeah, that was before deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: But of course, I think these ideas really found

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: their practical implementation in deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: What about the memory side of things?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: I think he was talking about knowledge representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Do you think about memory a lot?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: One way you can think of neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: as a kind of memory, you're memorizing things,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but it doesn't seem to be the kind of memory

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that's in our brains,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: or it doesn't have the same rich complexity,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: long-term nature that's in our brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: The brain is more of a sparse access memory

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: so that you can actually retrieve very precisely

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: like bits of your experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: The retrieval aspect, you can like introspect,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: you can ask yourself questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: You can program your own memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And language is actually the tool you use to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: I think language is a kind of operating system

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: for the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And use language, well, one of the uses of language

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: is as a query that you run over your own memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Use words as keys to retrieve specific experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: or specific concepts, specific thoughts.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Like language is a way you store thoughts,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: not just in writing, in the physical world,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but also in your own mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And it's also how you retrieve them.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Imagine if you didn't have language,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: then you would have to,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: you would not really have a self-internally triggered

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: way of retrieving past thoughts.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: You would have to rely on external experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: For instance, you see a specific sight,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: you smell a specific smell, and that brings up memories,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but you would not really have a way

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to deliberately access these memories without language.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Well, the interesting thing you mentioned

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: is you can also program the memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: You can change it, probably with language.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yeah, using language, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Well, let me ask you a Chomsky question,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: which is like, first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: do you think language is like fundamental?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Like there's turtles, what's at the bottom of the turtles?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: They don't go, it can't be turtles all the way down.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Is language at the bottom of cognition of everything?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Is language the fundamental aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: of what it means to be a thinking thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: No, I don't think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: I think language is-

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: You disagree with Noam Chomsky?

body.input: Yeah. It feels like there's a little bit of a gray area.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Because you're basically saying

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: But those abstractions do not seem to be effective

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: for generalizing far outside of the things that's already seen.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: But generalize a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yeah, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: No, deep learning does generalize a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Generalization is not binary, it's more like a spectrum.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And there's a certain point, it's a gray area,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but there's a certain point

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: where there's an impressive degree of generalization that happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: No, I guess exactly what you were saying is,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: intelligence is how efficiently you're able to generalize

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: far outside of the distribution of things you've seen already.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So it's both like the distance of how far you can,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: like how new, how radically new something is,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and how efficiently you're able to deal with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So you can think of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: as a measure of an information conversion ratio.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Like imagine a space of possible situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And you've covered some of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So you have some amount of information

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: about your space of possible situations

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that's provided by the situations you already know.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And that's, on the other hand, also provided by the prior knowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that the system brings to the table,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: the prior knowledge that's embedded in the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So the system starts with some information, right,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: about the problem, about the task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And it's about going from that information to a program,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: what we would call a skill program, a behavioral program,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that can cover a large area of possible situation space.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And essentially the ratio between that area

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and the amount of information you start with is intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So a very smart agent can make efficient uses

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: of very little information about a new problem

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and very little prior knowledge as well

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to cover a very large area of potential situations

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in that problem without knowing

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: what these future new situations are going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So one of the other big things you talk about in the paper,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: we've talked about a little bit already,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but let's talk about it some more, is actual tests of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So if we look at like human and machine intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: do you think tests of intelligence should be different

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: for humans and machines,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: or how we think about testing of intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Are these fundamentally the same kind of intelligences

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that we're after and therefore the tests should be similar?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So if your goal is to create AIs that are more human-like,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: then it will be super valuable, obviously,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to have a test that's universal,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that applies to both AIs and humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: so that you could establish a comparison between the two,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: that you could tell exactly how intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in terms of human intelligence, a given system is.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So that said, the constraints that apply to artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and to human intelligence are very different,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and your test should account for this difference,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: because if you look at artificial systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: it's always possible for an experimenter

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: to buy arbitrary levels of skill at arbitrary tasks,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: either by injecting hard-coded prior knowledge into the system,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: via rules and so on, that come from the human mind,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: from the minds of the programmers,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and also buying higher levels of skill just by training on more data.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: For instance, you could generate an infinity of different Go games,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and you could train a Go playing system that way,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: but you could not directly compare it to human Go playing skills,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: because a human that plays Go had to develop that skill

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in a very constrained environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: They had a limited amount of time, they had a limited amount of energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and of course, this started from a different set of priors,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: this started from innate human priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So I think if you want to compare the intelligence of two systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: in fact, the intelligence of an AI and the intelligence of a human,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: you have to control for priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: You have to start from the same set of knowledge priors about the task,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: and you have to control for experience, that is to say, for training data.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So what's priors?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: So prior is whatever information you have about a given task

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: before you start learning about this task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: And how's that different from experience?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Measures of Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #120

body.input: Well, experience is acquired.
