body.input: whether they are your parents, whether they are the state in which you happen to be born, whether they are somebody on the other side of planet Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can judge them if you have a standard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And my standard, and I think the right standard is human well-being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is, that which is good for human beings, qua human beings, is the standard by which we judge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I can say that certain periods of history were bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They happened. It's important to study them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's important to understand what they did that made them bad so we cannot do that again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I can say certain cultures, certain periods in time were good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Why? Because they promoted human well-being and human flourishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's the standard. And then derive from that, okay, what is it that made a particular culture good?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What is it that made that particular culture positive in terms of human well-being and human flourishing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What made this bad? And hopefully from that, I can derive a principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay, if I want human flourishing and human well-being in the future, I want to be more like these guys and less like those guys.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I want to derive what is the principle that will guide me in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's, I think, how human knowledge ultimately develops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think people often make a mistake just – I'm not saying you're wrong, but lots of people don't actually read the original sources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so what happens is people will attack conservatives, assuming that conservatives think that whatever comes from the past is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Actually, it's very difficult to find a thinker who actually says something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Selden or Burke, the big conservative theorists, Hooker, they're all people who understand that the tradition carries with it mistakes that were made in the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this is actually, I think, an important part of their empiricism is that they see the search for truth as something a society does by trial and error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what that means is that at any given moment, you have to be aware of the possibility that things that you've inherited are actually false.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the job of the political thinker or the jurist or the philosopher is not to dig in and say, you know, whatever it is that we've inherited is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The job is to look at the society as a whole and say, look, we have this job of, first of all, conservation, just making sure that we don't lose good things that we've had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And second, seeing if we can repair things in order to improve them where it's necessary or where it's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that process is actually a creative process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This is a way in which I think it is similar to your own philosophy that you take the inherited tradition and you look for a way that you can shape it in order to make it something better than it was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's a baseline for what we call conservatism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Just a comment. So the trial and error, the errors is you're proud of the errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's a feature, not a bug. So you mentioned trial and error a few times yesterday.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's a really interesting kind of idea. It's basically accepting that the journey is going to have flaws as opposed to saying, I mean, the conclusion there is the current system is flawed and it will always be flawed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It will always be flawed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And you try to improve it when you listen to your own talk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's much more of an optimism for the system being perfect now or potentially soon or could be perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And to me, the way I heard it is almost like accepting that the system is flawed and through trial and error will improve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And your aunt says, no, we can have a perfection now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's what it sounds to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah. And I think that's right. I think the difference is that at some point, just like in science, I think one can stop the trial and error and say, I can now see a pattern here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I can see that certain actions lead to bad consequences, certain actions lead to good consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Let me try to abstract away what is it that is good and what is it that is bad and build a system around what is good and reject what is bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think ultimately, if you read The Founding Fathers and whether we call them conservatives or individuals, what The Founding Fathers actually did, all of them, I think, is study history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They all did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They all talk about history. They all talk about examples of other cultures, whether they go back to the Republic in Venice or back to the ancient Greeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They studied these. They learned lessons from them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They try to figure out what has worked in the past and what hasn't and try to draw principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now, in my view, they got pretty close to what I would consider kind of an ideal, but they didn't get it completely right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Here we sit 200-something years after the Declaration and after the Constitution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think we can look back and say, okay, well, what did they get right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What did they get wrong based on how is it done and where are the flaws and we can improve on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think we can get closer to perfection and based on those kind of observations, based on that kind of abstraction, that kind of discovery of what is true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: just like at some point you do the experiments, you do the trial and error, and now you come up with a scientific principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It is true that 100 years later you might discover that, hey, I missed something, there's something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But to not take the full lesson, to insist on incrementalism, to insist on we're just going to tinker with the system instead of saying, no, there's something really wrong with having a king.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's something really wrong with not having any representation or whatever the standard needs to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In the name of we don't want to move too fast, I think is a mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the problem with trial and error in politics is that we're talking about human life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So there was a big trial around communism and 100 million people paid the price for the trial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I could have told them in advance, as did many people, that it would not work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There are principles of human nature, principles that we can study from history, principles about economics and other aspects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, we know it's not going to work. You don't need to try it again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We've had communal arrangements throughout history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There was an experiment with fascism and there have been experiments with all kinds of political systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay, we've done them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's sad that we did them because many of us knew they wouldn't work. We should learn the lesson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think that all of history now converges on one lesson, and that is what we need to do is build systems that protect individual freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is the core. That's what ultimately leads to human flourishing and human success and human achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And to the extent that we place anything above that individual, whether it's the state, whether it's the ethnicity, whether it's the race,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: whether it's the bourgeois, whatever it happens to be, a class or whatever, whenever we place something above the individual, the consequence or negative,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: that's one of these principles that I think we can derive from studying 3000 years of civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's tragic, I think, because we're going to keep experimenting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Sadly, I see it, right? I'm not winning this battle. I'm losing the battle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're going to keep experimenting with different forms of collectivism, and we're going to keep paying the price in human life

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and in missed opportunities for human flourishing and human success and human wealth and prosperity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, look, let's take communism as a good example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: None of the major conservative thinkers would say, you know, what's a good idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: A good idea would be to experiment by raising everything that we've inherited and starting from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, that's the conservative complaint or accusation against rationalists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, as opposed to empiricism, using rationalism, let's take Descartes kind of as a benchmark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can you also maybe define rationalism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah. These are two terms that are in philosophy, especially in epistemology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're often compared to one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Your own said that it's a false dichotomy, and maybe it is a bit exaggerated, but that doesn't mean it's not useful for conceptualizing the domain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So rationalist is somebody like Descartes who says, I'm going to set aside, I'm going to try to set aside everything I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: everything I've inherited, I'm going to start from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He explicitly says, you know, in evaluating the inheritance of the past, he explicitly says, you take a look at the histories that we have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: they're not reliable, you take a look at the moral and the scientific writings that we receive, they're not very good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: His baseline is to look very critically at the past and say, look, I'm evaluating it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think all in all, it's just not worth very much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Whatever I do, beginning from scratch, is going to be better as long as, and here's his caveat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: as long as I'm proceeding from self-evident assumptions, from self-evident premises, things that you can't argue against.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think, therefore, I am.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Right. And then from there, deducing what he calls infallible conclusions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So that model of self-evident premises to infallible conclusions, I'm calling that rationalism. I think that's kind of a standard academic jargon term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's opposed to empiricism, which is a thinker, I think, in universities, usually the empiricist is David Hume.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And David Hume will say, we can't learn anything the way that Descartes said. I mean, there is nothing that's that self-evident and that infallible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So Hume proposes, based on Newton and Boyle and the new physical sciences, so Hume proposes a science of man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the science of man sounds an awful lot like what Youran just said, which is we're going to take a look at human nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: at the nature of societies, human nature, we're going to try to abstract towards fixed principles for describing it, human societies, we're going to try to do the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And from there we get, for example, contemporary economics, but we also get sociology and anthropology, which cut in a different direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So that's rationalism versus empiricism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can I just say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah, go ahead, please.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah, I agree with that. I think empiricism, the one thing I disagree is I think empiricism rarely comes to these abstractions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, they want more facts. It's always about collecting more evidence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But this is where I think Ayn Rand is so unusual and where I think there's something new here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that's a bold statement given the history of philosophy, but I think Ayn Rand is something new.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so she says, yes, we agree about rationalism and that's inherently wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Empiricism has the problem of, okay, where does it lead?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You never come to a conclusion. You're just accumulating evidence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's something in addition, there's a third alternative, which she is positing, which is using empirical evidence, not denying empirical evidence, recognizing that there are some axioms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's some axioms that we all, at the base of all of our knowledge, that are starting points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're not rejecting axiomatic knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And integrating those two and identifying the fact that based on these axioms and based on these empirical evidence, we can come to truths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Just again, like we do in science, we have certain axioms, scientific axioms, we have certain experiments that we want, and then we can come to some identification of a truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that truth is always going to be challenged by new information, by new knowledge, but as long as that's what we know, that is what truth is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The truth is contextual in the sense that it's contextual, it's based on that knowledge that surrounds it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's okay for it to change if you get new facts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Absolutely. It's always available to change if the facts that you get, and they really are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, the burden of changing what you've come to, a conclusion of truth, is high, so you'd have to have real evidence that it's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But that happens all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So it happens in science, right? We discovered that what we thought was true is not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it can happen in politics and ethics even more so than in science because they're much messier fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But the idea is that you can come to a truth, but it's not just deductive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Most truths are inductive. We learn from observing reality and, again, coming to principles about what works and what's not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And here I think this is, Ayn Rand is different. She doesn't fall into the, and she's different in her politics and she's different in her epistemology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: She doesn't fall into the conventional view. She's an opponent of Hume and she's an opponent of Descartes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: She's certainly an opponent of Kant's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think she's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If it's okay, can we walk back to criticism of communism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You're both critics of communism and socialism. Why did communism fail?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You started to say that conservatives criticize it on the basis of rationalism, that you're throwing away the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You're starting from scratch. Is that the fundamental description of why communism failed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think the fundamental difference between rationalists and empiricists is the question of whether you're throwing away the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's the argument. And it cashes out as a distinction between abstract universal rationalist political theories and empirical political theories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Empirical political theories are, they're always going to say something like, look, there are many different societies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can say that some are better and some are worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But the problem is that there are many different ways in which a society can be better or worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's an ongoing competition. And we're learning on an ongoing basis what are the ways in which societies can be better and worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That creates a kind of, I'd say, a mild skepticism, a moderate skepticism among conservatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't think too many conservatives have a problem looking at the Soviet Union, which is brutal and murderous, ineffective in its economics, totally ineffective spiritually, and then collapsed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay. So I think it's easier for us to look at a system like that and say, you know, what on earth? What should we learn from that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But the main conservative tradition is pretty tolerant of a diversity of different kinds of society and is slow to insist that France is so tyrannical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It just needs a revolution because what's going to come after the revolution is going to be much better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The assumption is that there's lots of things that are good about most societies and that a clean slate leads you to throw out all of the inherited things that you don't even know how to notice until they're gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Could I actually play a double's advocate here and address something you also said?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can we, as opposed to knowing the empirical data of the 20th century that communism presented, can we go back to the beginning of the 20th century?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can you empathize or steel man or put yourself in a place of the Soviet Union where the workers are being disrespected?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And can you not see that the conservatives could be pro-communism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Like communism is such a strongly negative word in modern day political discourse that you can't like you have to put yourself in the mind of people who like red colors, who like it was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's all about the branding, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But also like the ideas of solidarity, of nation, of togetherness, of respect for fellow man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean all of these things that kind of communism represents, can you not see that this idea is actually going along with conservatism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In some ways respecting the deep ideals of the past, but proposing a new way to raise those ideals, implement those ideals in the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes, I'm going to try to do what you're suggesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But historically we actually have a more useful option, I think, for both of our positions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Instead of pretending that we like the actual communists, we have conservative statesmen like Disraeli and Bismarck who initiated social legislation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The first step towards saying, look, we're one nation, we're undergoing industrialization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That industrialization is important and positive, but it's also doing a lot of damage to a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In particular, it's doing damage not just to individuals and families, but it's doing damage to the social fabric, the capacity of Britain or German to remain cohesive society as it is being harmed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's these two conservative statesmen, Disraeli and Bismarck, who actually take the first steps in order to legislate for what today we would consider to be minimal social programs, pensions and disability insurance and those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: For sure, conservatives do look at industrialization as a rapid change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They say, we do have to care about the nation as a whole and we have to care about it as a unity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I assume that your own will say, look, that's the first step towards the catastrophe of communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But before your own drives that nail into the coffin, let me try to make a distinction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because when you read Marx, you're reading an intellectual descendant of Descartes. You're reading somebody who says, look, every society consists of oppressors and oppressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's an improvement in some ways over liberal thinking because at least he's seeing groups as a real social phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But he says every society has an oppressor class and oppressed class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There are different classes, there are different groups, and whenever one is stronger, it exploits the ones that are weaker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is the foundation of a revolutionary political theory. Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because the moment that you say that the only relationship between the stronger and the weaker is exploitation, the moment that you say that, then you're pushed into the position.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And Marx and Engels say this explicitly. You're pushed into the position.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think when will the exploitation end? Never until there's a revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What happens when there's a revolution? You eliminate the oppressor class. It's annihilationist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, you can immediately when you read it see why it's different from Descartes or Bismarck because they're trying to keep everybody somehow at peace with one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And Marx is saying there is no peace. That oppressor class has to be annihilated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then they go ahead and do it and they kill 100 million people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I do think that despite the fact your question is good and right, there are certain similarities and concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But still, I think you can tell the difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That extra step of revolution to you is where the problem comes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Like that extra step of let's kill all the oppressors. That's the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then to you, you're on the whole step one is the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, it's all a problem. First, I don't view communism as something that radical in a sense that I think it comes from a tradition of collectivism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think it comes from a tradition of looking at groups and measuring things in terms of groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It comes from tradition where you expect some people to be sacrificed for the greater good of the whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think it comes from a tradition where mysticism, a revelation as the source of truth is accepted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I view Marx as in some sense very Christian. I don't think he's this radical rejecting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think he's just reformatting Christianity in a sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In a sense, he's replacing God with the proletarian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Knowledge, you have to get knowledge from somewhere. So you need the dictatorship of the proletarian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You need somebody, the Stalin, the Lenin, who somehow communes with the spirit, the spirit of the proletarian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's no rationality, not rationalism. There's no rationality in Marx.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There is a lot of mysticism and there is a lot of hand waving and there's a lot of sacrifice and a lot of original sin in the way he views humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I view Marx as one more collectivist in a whole string of collectivists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I know less about Disraeli, so I'll focus on Bismarck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Bismarck is really responding to political pressures from the left and he's responding to the rise of communism, socialism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But what Bismarck is doing, he's putting something alternative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He's presenting an alternative to the proletarian as the standard by which we should we should matter the good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what he's replacing it is the state. He's replacing the proletarian with the state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that has exactly the same problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is, first, it requires sacrificing some to others, which is what the welfare state basically legitimizes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It places the state above all, so the state now becomes, I think, the biggest evil of Bismarck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I definitely view him as a negative force in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Is public education. I mean, the Germans really dig in on public education and really develop it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And really the American model of public education is copying the German, the Prussian Bismarckian public education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can you speak to that real quick? Why the public education is such a root of moral evil for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, because it now says that there's one standard, and that standard is determined by government, by bureaucracy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: by whatever the government deems is in the national interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And Bismarck is very explicit about this. He's training the workers of the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They need to catch up with England and other places, and they need to train the workers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he's going to train some people to be the managerial classes, he's going to train other people to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he decides, right, the government, the bureaucracy is going to decide who's who and where they go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's no individual choice. There's no individual showing an ability to break out of what the government has decided is their little box.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's very little freedom. There's very little, you know, ultimately there's very little competition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's very little innovation. And this is the problem we have today in American education, which we can get to, is there's no competition and no innovation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We have one standard fit all, and then we have conflicts about what should be taught.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the conflicts now are not pedagogical. They're not about what works and what doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Nobody cares about that. It's about political agendas, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's about what my group wants to be taught and what that group wants to be taught, rather than actually discovering how do we get kids to read?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, we all know how to get kids to read, but there's a political agenda about not teaching phonics, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So a lot of schools don't teach phonics, even though the kids will never learn how to read properly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So it becomes politics. And I don't believe politics belongs in education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think education is a product. It's a service. And we know how to deliver products and services really, really efficiently at a really, really low price at a really, really high quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that's leaving it to the market to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But your fundamental criticism is that the state can use education to further its authoritarian aims.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, or whatever the aims. I mean, think about the conservative today critique of American educational system. It's dominated by the left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah. What did you expect? Right. If you leave it up to the state to fund, they're going to fund the things that promote state growth and state intervention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the left is better at that. It has been better at that than the right. And they now dominate our educational institutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But look, if we go back to Bismarck, my problem is placing the state above the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So if communism places the class above the individual, what matters is class individuals are nothing. They're cogs in a machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Bismarck, certainly the German tradition, much more than the British tradition or the American tradition, the German tradition is to place the state above the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that's equally evil. And the outcome is fascism. And the outcome is the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The outcome is the deaths of tens of millions of people when taken to its ultimate conclusion, just like socialism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The ultimate conclusion of it is communism, nationalism in that form, kind of the Bismarckian form, the ultimate conclusion is Nazism or some form of fascism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because you don't care about the individual. The individual doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think this is one of the differences in the Anglo-American tradition where the Anglo-American tradition, even the conservatives have always acknowledged.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it goes back to a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Especially the conservatives. The conservatives were there first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They acknowledged. Well, you've defined conservatives to include all the good thinkers of the distant past. And they're all good thinkers. We agree on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm defining conservatism the way that Burke does. I'm just... Look, this is a very simple observation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Burke thinks when you open Burke and you actually read him, he starts naming all of these people who he's defending.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's bizarre. I'm sorry. It's just intellectual sloppiness for people to be publishing books called Burke, the first conservative, the founding conservative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, this is nonstop. It's a view that says Burke reacts to the French Revolution. So conservatism has no prior tradition. It's just reacting to the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this is just absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can I ask a quick question on conservatism? Are there any conservatives that are embracing of revolutions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So are they ultimately against the concept of revolution?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes. Burke himself embraces the Polish Revolution, which takes place almost exactly at the same time as the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the argument's really interesting because there's a common mistake is assuming that Burke and conservative thinkers are always in favor of slow change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that's also just factually mistaken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Burke is against the French Revolution because he thinks that there are actually tried and true things that work, things that work for human flourishing and freedom included as a very important part of human flourishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He, like many others, takes the British, the English Constitution to be a model of something that works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So it has a king. It has various other things that maybe your own will say, well, that's a mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But still, for centuries, it's the leader in many things that I think we can easily agree are human flourishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And Burke says, look, what's wrong with the French Revolution?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What's wrong with the French Revolution is that they have a system that has all sorts of problems, but they could be repairing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And instead, what they're doing by overthrowing everything is they're moving away from what we know is good for human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Then he looks at the Polish Revolution and he says the Poles do the opposite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The Poles have a non-functioning traditional constitution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's too democratic. It's impossible to raise armies and to defend the country because of the fact that every nobleman has a veto.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So the Polish Revolution moves in the direction of the British Constitution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They repair their constitution through a quick, a rapid revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They install a king along the model that looks a lot like Britain. And Burke supports it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He says this is a good revolution. So it's not the need to quickly make a change in order to save yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's not what conservatives are objecting to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What they're objecting to is instead of looking at experience in order to try to make a slow or quick improvement, a measured improvement to achieve a particular goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: instead of doing that, you say, look, the whole thing has just been wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what we've really got to do is annihilate a certain part of the population and then make completely new laws and a completely new theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's what he's objecting to. That's the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that then becomes the model for communist revolutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And for me, I mean, the French Revolution is clearly a real evil and wrong, but it's not that it was a revolution and it's not that it tried to change everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, let's remember what was going on in France at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, people were starving and the monarchy in particular was completely detached, completely detached from the suffering of the people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And something needed to change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The unfortunate thing is that the change was motivated by an egalitarian philosophy, not egalitarian in the sense that I think the Fanny Fathers talked about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but egalitarian in a sense of real equality, quality of outcome, motivated by a philosophy, by Rousseau's philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And inevitably, you could tell that the ideas were going to lead to this, to massive destruction and death and annihilation of a class.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can't, annihilation is never an option.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is, it's not true that a good revolution never leads to mass death of just whole groups of people because a good revolution is about the sanctity of the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's about preservation, liberty of the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And again, that goes back to, and the French Revolution denies and Rousseau denies really that in civilization there is a value and a thing called the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think this is a good place to have this discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The Fanny Fathers of the United States, are they individualists or are they conservatives?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So in this particular revolution that founded this country, at the core of which are some fascinating, some powerful ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: were those founding fathers, were those ideas coming from a place of conservatism or did they put primary value into the freedom and the power of the individual?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There were both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, this is something that's a little bit difficult for sometimes for Americans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, even very educated Americans, they talk about the founding fathers as though it's kind of like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Monolith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah, this collective entity with a single brain and a single value system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I think at the time, that's not the way any of them saw it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So roughly there's two camps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And they map onto the rationalist versus traditionalist empiricist dichotomy that I proposed earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so on the one hand, you have real revolutionaries like Jefferson and Paine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These are the people who Burke was writing against.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These are the people who supported the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So when you say real, so when you say Paine, you're referring to revolutionaries in a bad way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Like this is a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These are people who will say history up until now has been, you know, with Descartes, but applied to politics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: history up until now has been, you know, just a story of ugliness, foolishness, stupidity and evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And if you apply reason, we'll all come to roughly, we'll all come to the same conclusions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, and Paine writes a book called The Age of Reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And The Age of Reason is a manifesto for here is the answer to political and moral problems throughout history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We have the answers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's in the same school as Rousseau's The Social Contra- no, you don't like that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, no, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Oh, I thought it was-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think they're the opposites.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Just to throw in a question on Jefferson and Paine, do you think America would exist without those two figures?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So like how important is spice in the flavor of the dish you're making?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't want to try to run the counterfactual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, I don't have confidence that I know the answer to the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But it's so much fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm going to offer something that I think is more fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: More fun than the counterfactual is America had two revolutions, not one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: At first, there is a revolution that is strongly spiced with this kind of rationalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then there's a 10-year period after the Declaration of Independence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's a 10-year period under which America has a constitution, its first constitution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: which today they call the Articles of the Confederation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But there's a constitution from 1777.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that constitution is based on, in a lot of ways, on the hottest new ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It has, instead of the traditional British system with a division of powers between an executive and a bicameral legislature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: instead of that traditional English model which most of the states had as their governments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: instead of that they say, no, we're going to have one elected body, okay, and that body, that Congress,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: it's going to be the executive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's going to be the legislative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's going to be everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's going to run as a big committee.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These are the ideas of the French Revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You get to actually see them implemented in Pennsylvania, in the Pennsylvania Constitution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and then later in the National Assembly in France.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's a disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The thing doesn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's completely made up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's not based on any kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's neither based on historical experience, nor is it based on historical custom, on what people are used to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what they succeed in creating with this first constitution is it's wonderfully rational, but it's a complete disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It doesn't allow the raising of taxes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It doesn't allow the mustering of troops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It doesn't allow giving orders to soldiers to fight a war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And if that had continued, if that had continued to be the American Constitution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: America never would have been an independent country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They aren't willing to do that counterfactual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What happens during those years where Washington and Jay and Knox and Hamilton and Morris,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: there's like this group of conservatives, they're mostly soldiers and lawyers other than Washington.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Most of them are from northern cities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this group is much more conservative than the Tom Paine and Jefferson School.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Some historians call them the Nationalist Party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Historically, they give up the word nationalism and they call themselves the Federalists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But they're basically the Nationalist Party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It means on the one hand that their goal is to create an independent nation, independent from Britain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But on the other hand, they believe that they already have national legal traditions, the common law,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the forms of government that have been imported from Britain, and of course Christianity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: which they consider to be part of their inheritance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This Federalist Party is the Conservative Party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These are people who are extremely close in ideas to Burke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And these are people who wrote the Constitution of the United States, the second Constitution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the second revolution in 1787 when Washington leads the establishment of a new Constitution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: which maybe technically legally it wasn't even legal under the old Constitution, but it was democratic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what it did is it said, we're going to take what we know about English government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: what we've learned by applying English government in the states, we're going to create a national government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: a unified national government that's going to muster power in its hands, enough power to be able to do things

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: like fighting wars to defend a unified people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Those are conservatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now, it's reasonable to say, well, look, there was no king, so how conservative could they be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I think that's a reasonable question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But don't forget that the American colonies, the English colonies in America by that point had been around for 150 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They had written constitutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They had already adapted for an entire century, adapted the English Constitution to local conditions

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: where there's no aristocracy and there's no king.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think you can see that as a positive thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: On the other hand, they have slavery. That's an innovation. That's not English.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So it's a little bit different from the English Constitution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But those men are conservatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They make the minimum changes that they need to the English Constitution, and they largely replicate it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: which is why the Jeffersonians hated them so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They call them apostates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They say they've betrayed equality and liberty and fraternity by adopting an English-style Constitution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I would imagine, Yoram, you would put emphasis of the success of the key ideas at the founding of this country elsewhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: at the freedom of the individual, as opposed to the tradition of the British Empire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, the one thing I agree with, Yoram, is the fact that, yes, the founding fathers were not a monolith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, they argued, they debated, they disagreed, they wrote against each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256
