body.input: that I would like people to be able to voluntarily choose both in and out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I'd like to see people be able to go and join that group

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: that they believe will allow for the pursuit of happiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But let me say that, you know, that's a description of an ideal, what I'm just saying, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I recognize that that's not the reality in which we live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I recognize that that's not the reality in which history...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: History, you know, recognizing that such as that the individual exists in a sense philosophically

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: is a massive achievement, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, human beings, however they evolved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: clearly we started out in a tribal context in which the individual didn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We followed the leader. The competition was for power, power over the group

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and dictates how the group should work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, the history of human beings is a history of gaining knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And part of the knowledge is the value of an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And you can see that in religion, you can see that in philosophy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you can see that through the evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then, you know, we evolved from tribes into nations

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and then empires and conflicts between nations and conflicts between empires.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And we tried a lot of different things, if you will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't think we always did it on purpose, but we kind of did different philosophies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: different sets of ideas drove us towards different collectives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: different groupings and different ways in which to structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And after, I don't know, 3000 years of kind of known history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: it's history before that, but we don't know much about it, 3000 years of known history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you can sit back and evaluate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think that's what is done in the Enlightenment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And you sit back and suddenly we can do it today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can sit back and evaluate what promotes human flourishing and what doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what do we mean by human flourishing? Who's flourishing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, individual human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Since I don't believe in a zero-sum world and the world is not zero-sum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: we can see that it's empirically possible to show that the world is not a zero-sum game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: My flourishing doesn't come at your expense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I can show that a system that promotes my flourishing probably promotes your flourishing as well

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and promotes the general welfare in that sense because it promotes individuals flourishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And we can look at all these examples of how we evolved

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and what leads to bloodshed and what doesn't and what promotes this ability to flourish as an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Again, an achievement, the idea of individual flourishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then we can think about how to create a political system around that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: a political system that recognizes and allows for the formation of groups,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but just under the principle of voluntary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can't be forced to join a group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can't be cursed into forming a group

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: other than the fact that you're born in a particular place, in a particular, you know, that in a sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But that's not forced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's a difference between metaphysics and between choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So this is something that came up in the debate that Yoram said that not all human relations are voluntary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And you kind of emphasize that a lot of where we are is not voluntary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're grounded. We're connected in so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So how can a human be free in the way you're describing individual be free

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: if some part of who we are is not voluntary, some part of who we are as other people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, because what do we mean by freedom?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Freedom doesn't mean the negation of the laws of physics, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Freedom doesn't mean ignoring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Freedom means the ability within the scope of what's available for you to choose, being able to choose those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So in a political context, freedom means the absence of coercion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So once you're an adult, you know, Yoram says you're born into a particular religious context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Absolutely. But once you're an adult, I think it's incumbent on you to evaluate that religious context

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and look at different religions or non-religion or whatever and choose your philosophy of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Choose your values. Choose how you want to live your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's the freedom. The freedom is one system says you're either cursed by the state or cursed by the group

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: or cursed by society around you to follow a particular path or the expectation is, the demand is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the pressure is to conform to a particular path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And my view is, no, you should be in a position to be able to choose your path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that choice means you look around, you evaluate, you evaluate based on history, based on knowledge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: based on all of these things, and you choose what that path would be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's fundamentally what freedom means. Yes, you cannot choose your parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But of course not. Nobody would claim that that's within the scope of what is possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think the coercion, freedom dichotomy, these are too few concepts, coercion and freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's too simplistic to be able to describe what we're actually dealing with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The traditional Anglo-conservative view is that society has to be, it has to be ordered, it has to be disciplined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And there are two choices for how it can be ordered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: One is that a people is, by its own traditions, you would say voluntarily, but these are mostly inherited traditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: By its own traditions, it is ordered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: For example, people just in general will not go into somebody else's yard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: because that's the custom here is we don't go into somebody else's yard without their permission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so Fortescue, we're talking about 500 years ago already.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So Fortescue says that the genius of the English people is that our government can be mild

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and apply very little coercion because the people are so disciplined.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now when he says the people are so disciplined, what he's saying is that our nation, our tribes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: we have strong traditions which channel people through tools of being honored and dishonored.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now that's a reality that exists in every society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's not captured by your distinction between coercion and lack of coercion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: When I'm going to be dishonored if I don't care for my aging mother,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm not being coerced like the state comes and puts a gun to my head, but I am being pressured and given guidelines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm saying that's wrong and I'm saying that's dangerous because that could easily be used for bad traditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, of course it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But what's the standard by which we evaluate what a good tradition is, a bad tradition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You're getting to the standard too fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: First I want to know factually, is it true that all societies work like this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because if it's true that all societies work like this, then saying we should be free from it is just a fantasy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, A, I don't think all societies work like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think much of what happened in America post-founding in the 19th century didn't work like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that's the genius of America.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think what happened during the 19th century in the Industrial Revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: what happened in the 19th century to some extent globally, but certainly in the United States didn't work that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It broke tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think all innovation breaks tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think that's what the genius of this country is and the post-enlightenment world is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think pre that tradition, they worked that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And then the question is, do people understand why they do what they do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is, I don't want people doing what I think is right just because I think it's right and I've created a society in which, yeah, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Somebody founded this country in a particular way, so we're just going to follow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I want people to understand what they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I want people to have a respect for property, not because it's a tradition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but because they understand the value of a respect for property.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I want people not to murder one another, not because it's a commandment, that shall not murder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but because they have an understanding of why murdering is bad and wrong and bad for them and bad for the kind of world that they want to live in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think that's what we achieve through enlightenment, through education,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and where we don't treat people just as a blob, a tribe that just follows orders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but we now treat individuals as capable of thinking for themselves, capable for discovering truth, capable of figuring out their own values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that's the big break between, and this is why, you know, this is the break I think that the declaration represents,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the break between society that is based on tradition, following commandments, following rules, because they are the rules, because they are the commandments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and a society where individuals understand those rules, understand, yes, it's now become a tradition, let's say, to respect individual rights, to respect property rights,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but they're not following it because it's a tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're following it because they understand what it is about it that makes it good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So that's the world I think that we were on the process of evolving towards,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and that is what got destroyed in the 20th century and has certainly disappeared today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think that's a great tragedy is that we're evolving to a place where people understood the values that represent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And of course, the danger with tradition is, I mean, well, agree, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's, yeah, it's okay to kill the Jew, right, or it's okay to steal people's property if they're of a certain color, it's okay to enslave.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Those are all traditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And yet, once you stop and say, but what are they based on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Is this right? Is this just based on some moral law?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, it's not. There's something wrong here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can't achieve happiness and success if we follow these.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You're talking about reason and tradition, but I think I would love to sort of linger on the stickiness of humans that you describe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you kind of said this primary, the individuals is primary and that was a great invention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But to me, it's not at all obvious that somehow that the invention that humans have been practicing for a very long time of the stickiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: of community, of family, of love, that's not obvious to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's not also fundamental to human flourishing and should be celebrated and protected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Of course it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now, I suppose the argument you're making is when you start to let the state define what the stickiness, how the stickiness looks between humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you're really like the voluntary aspect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I just want to sort of the observation is humans seem to be pretty happy when they form communities, however you define that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So romantic partnership, family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Some communities, some communities, people are miserable in other communities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So the nature of the community matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We know this. We know that some bondings are not healthy and not good for the individuals involved and they don't thrive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I absolutely, I mean, I'm a lover, not a fighter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm a huge believer in love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The whole philosophy I think is a love-based philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I fight in order to love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So love is at the core of all of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's a love of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's a love of the world out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's a love of other people because they represent a value to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So the stickiness is there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: My point is A, it should be chosen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It should be consciously chosen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this is, put aside the state, forget the state for a minute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Forget corrosion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Forget all that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What I would encourage individuals to do, and this is where I'm not primarily a political, interested in politics, although I tend to talk most about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm primarily interested in human beings and how they live in a sense in morality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what I would urge individuals to do is to think about their relationships, to choose the best relationships possible, but to seek out great relationships because other human beings are an immense value to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And, you know, when I write, you know, maybe you won't quote it this or not, but I write that, you know, about the trade of principle and trading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, it's easy and obvious to think of it as a materialistic kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, I do the chores this day and my wife does the chores the other day and we're trading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But trading is much more subtle than that and can be much more spiritual than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's about the trading in emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's about the way one sees each other, what one gets from one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think friendship is a form of trade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now, I know that that seems to make it material, but I don't think it's of trade as a material thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But friendship is incredibly important in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Love is incredibly important in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, having a group of friends is incredibly important in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: All of these are sticky and important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: OK. How can I try to be eloquent on this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So if you give people freedom, if you give people...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Politics, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, not politics, relations, relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So this is interesting because we have an interesting dynamic going on here in terms of beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're differing and there's interesting overlaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But there's a worry if you look at human history and you study lessons of history and you look at modern society,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: if you give people freedom in terms of stickiness and human relations and so on, full...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Like if you not give people freedom, emphasize freedom as the highest ideal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's the way. So you have to study what actually happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If you emphasize that the stickiness, the bonds of humans is holding you back,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the exercise of voluntary choice is the highest ideal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the danger of that is for that to be implemented or interpreted in certain kinds of ways by us flawed humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: that are not... I mean, you could say we're perfectly reasonable and rational.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can think through all of our decisions, but really, I mean, especially when you're young,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you get horny and you make decisions that are suboptimal perhaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So the point is you have to look at reality of when you emphasize different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So when you talk about what is the ideal life, what is the ideal relations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you have to also think like, what are you emphasizing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think you both agree on what's important, that community can be important, that freedom is important,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but what are you emphasizing? And you're really emphasizing the individual

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and you're emphasizing, you're, Ram, you're emphasizing more of the community,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: of the family, of the stickiness of the nation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, look, I don't want to deny the place of the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that there really is a very great change in civilization when the books of Moses

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: announce that the individual is created in the image of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's a step that's, as far as we know, without precedent before that in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And to a very large degree, I mean, one of the kind of unspoken things going on is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yaron and I really do agree on all sorts of things, I think in part because we're both Jewish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, I said he was channeling Moses, but that's still in my book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's still pretty impressive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, that's a compliment. I took it to the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: For me, that's a compliment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And we'll talk about this a little bit just for the listener, just so they know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yaron, amongst many things, will talk about the virtue of nationalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but you're also a religious scholar of sorts, or at least leverage the Bible for much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: not much, but some of the wisdom in your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Look, the way that Yaron looks at enlightenment or maybe at Ayn Rand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: that's the way that I see the Hebrew scripture and the tradition that comes from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It has the same kind of place in my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I don't know how much we want to explore it, but I think that the agreement that we do have

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: about the positive value of the creative individual, the positive value of the individual's desire

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: to improve the world, and in my book that means including his or her desire to improve his family,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: his tribe, his congregation, his nation, but it still comes from this kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: for what Yaron calls selfishness, the desire to make things better for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In Hebrew Bible and in Judaism, that just is a positive thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Of course, it can be taken too far, but it just is positive, and it doesn't carry these kinds of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you know, you should turn the other cheek, you should give away your cloak, you should love your enemy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: These kinds of Christian tropes do not exist in Judaism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so it just, I like listening to Yaron's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I do feel like he goes too far on various things, but I also hear underneath that I can sort of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you know, hear the Jewish current and the resistance to things about Christianity that Jews often find.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Can I ask you a question there? Can you make an argument for turn the other cheek?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No.

body.input: I tend to, I guess you would equate that with altruism. I tend to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Injustice. It's unjust to turn the other cheek.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You don't love yourself if you're turning the other cheek. It's a lack of love, lack of self-respect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, let me push back on that because I like turn the other cheek, especially on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I like block the offender on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, so Twitter aside is more like you're investing in the long-term version of yourself versus the short-term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So that's the way I think about it. It's like the energy you put onto the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The turning out the cheek philosophy allows you to walk through the fire gracefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's some sense. I mean, perhaps you would reframe that as not a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Then that's not being altruistic or whatever, but there is something pragmatic about that kind of approach to life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Disciplining yourself so that you become a better version of yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Not only do we agree, but I think every religious and philosophical tradition probably has a version of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Even Kant, who we join together in finding to be terrible, even Kant makes that distinction between the short-term interest and the long-term interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I think that's universal. I don't know of anybody who's really disagreeing about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The thing that we were talking about a couple of minutes ago before we got onto this tangent is the relationship between the individual who is in the image of God and is of value as an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Nevertheless, there's this question about what is good for that person and also what makes him happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm not sure that those are exactly the same things, but they're both certainly relevant and important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think we're beginning to uncover this empirical disagreement about what it is that's good for the individual and what it is that makes him happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'll go back to something I raised in the debate, which is this theory of Durkheim that now has been popularized by Jordan Peterson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Durkheim argues that he's writing a book on suicide. He's trying to understand what brings individuals to suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He coins this term, I know me, lack of law. The argument is that individuals basically are healthy and happy when they find their place in a hierarchy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Within a loyalty group in a certain place in a hierarchy, they compete and struggle in order to rise in the hierarchy, but they know where they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They know who they are. The kids today like to say they know what their identity is because they associate themselves, their self-expansed to take on the leadership, the different layers, the past and the future of this particular hierarchy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I completely agree with Yaron that some of these hierarchies are pernicious and oppressive and terrible, and some of them are better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What we might disagree about is that you can find human beings who are capable of becoming healthy and happy off by themselves without participating in this kind of structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The minute that you accept, if you accept, that this is empirical reality about human beings, it's an iron law. You can't do anything. You can tell human beings that they can be free of all constraints, all you want, and you can get them to do things that, as you say, dissolve their place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They can have contempt for hierarchies. They can say, I'm not going to serve the man. I'm just going to burn them all down. You can get kids to say all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can get them either to be Marxists who are actively trying to overthrow and destroy the existing hierarchies, or you can make them some kind of liberal where they basically pretend the hierarchies don't exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They just act like they're not there. In both cases, and it's not a coincidence that that's what universities teach, is your choice is either Marxist revolution or liberal ignoring of the hierarchies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In both cases, what you've done is you've eliminated the possibility that the young person will be able to find his or her place in a way that allows them to grow and exercise their love, their drive, their creativity in order to advance something constructive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You've eliminated it, and you've put the burden on them, kind of a Nietzschean burden, to just be the fountain of all values yourself, which maybe some people can do it, but almost no one can do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that's empirically true. I think by telling them about their freedom rather than telling them about the need to join into some traditionalist hierarchy that can be good and healthy for them, I think we're destroying them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think we're destroying this generation and the last one and the next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Vjarrán is the burden of freedom destroying mankind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What freedom? I mean, how many people are indeed free? Look, the problem is that we're caught up on political concepts, and we're moving into ethical issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't think it's right to tell people, you're free, go do whatever the hell you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Just use your emotions, just go where you want to go in the spur of the moment. Think short term, don't think long term, but don't think. Why think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: One has to provide moral guidance, and morality here is crucial and crucially important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Part of taking responsibility for your own life is establishing a moral framework for your life. What does it mean to live a good life? That's much more important in a sense of a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It is my belief that people can do that. They can find and choose the values necessary to achieve a good life, but they need guidance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This is why religion evolved in my view, because people need guidance. I had called religion a primitive form of philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It was the original philosophy that provided people with some guidance about what to do and what not to do, and secular philosophy is supposed to do the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The problem is that I think religion and 99% of secular philosophy give people bad advice about what to do, and therefore they do bad stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Sometimes, because when they do good stuff it gets reinforced, we survive in spite of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Ideas like Kant and Hegel and Marx give young people awful advice about how to live and what to do, and as a consequence really bad stuff happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The world in which we exist today, in which we agree there are a lot of pathologies to it, there are a lot of bad stuff going on, in my view is going the wrong way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: In my view, a product of a set of ideas, on the one hand I think Christian ideas, on the other hand I think secular philosophical ideas, that have driven this country and the world more generally in a really bad direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This is why I do what I do, because I think at the core of it, the only way to change it is not to impose a new set of ideas from the top, because I worry about who's going to be doing the imposition, plus I don't believe you can force people to be good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's to challenge the ideas, it's to question the ideas, it's to present an alternative view of morality, an alternative set of moral principles, and ultimately an alternative view of political principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But it has to start with morality. If you don't, and my morality is centered on the individual and what the individual should do with his life in order to attain a good life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I believe that leads to happiness, but the good life, that's why it's good, right? The goal is survival and thriving and flourishing and happiness ultimately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But politics is a servant of that in the end. It's not an end in itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So the real issue is, you know, you asked before, what is the value of relationship? There's an enormous value in relationship because we get values from other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We don't produce all our values. We don't produce all our spiritual values, and we don't produce all our material values. Other people are a massive benefit to us because they produce values we can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's a massive division of labor in terms of values, not just in economics, but also in philosophy and elsewhere. It's why we have teachers. It's why we have moral teachers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Moral teachers are important to help guide us towards a good life. Not all of us are philosophers. But what I do demand, if you all are individuals, this is where I put a burden on people, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Understand what you're doing, right? You know, don't embrace a moral teaching because it was tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Don't embrace a moral teaching because your parents embraced it. Don't embrace a moral teaching just because your teachers are teaching it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Challenge it. Think about it. Embrace it because you embrace it. You might be wrong. You might embrace the wrong one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But take moral responsibility. Take responsibility over your life by evaluating, testing, challenging what you have received and choosing what you're going to pursue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I acknowledge empirically that most people don't do that. And this is why intellectual leadership is so important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This is why you want the voices in a culture to be good voices so that those people who don't think for themselves end up being followers, but they end up being followers of somebody good versus followers of somebody bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But for the thinkers in the world out there who I think are the people who count, who are the people who shape society, boy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, no, shape society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Wait a minute. Not count in a sense that you can dismiss the lives of others because obviously I'm anti-coercive and anti-violent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They sound like Plato.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes. I don't want to sound like Plato. But in a sense that they're the ones who end up shaping the world. They're the ones who end up shaping how the world is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I want those people to make choices about their values and not to just accept them based on tradition or based on commandment or based on where they happen to grow up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And in that sense, again, I do, and this is an interesting point where we disagree, but I'm not exactly sure what your own position is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I do believe in universal values. That is, there are things that are good and there are things that are evil. And I think we'd agree on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And there are systems. We agree that communism and fascism are evil. Well, I think we should be able to agree that some things, some political systems are good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And maybe there's this middle ground where we both think that they're not particularly bad, not particularly good, and you might think that they're better than I think they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But if we can agree on this is good and this is evil, then the systems that tend towards the good are good and the systems that tend towards the evil are evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But that's universal, right? I look at places like South Korea, Japan, Asia, cultures that are very, very different in many respects in the West.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And yet when they adopt certain Western ideas about freedom, about liberty, about individualism, I mean, the Japanese Constitution, because MacArthur forced it in there, has the pursuit of happiness in the Constitution, not because they chose it because he put it in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But they to some extent adopted that and they're successful. They're successful places today. Those societies in Asia that didn't adopt these values are not successful societies today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yaron, Japan has a birth rate of 1.1, 1.2 children per woman. I mean, look, there are some places where you give people freedom. This is also biblical, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The idea that everyone did what's right in his own eyes. Okay, right? This is a refrain in the book of judges. And the Bible is not an anti-freedom book. I mean, there's many, many.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Look, I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, we're not fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We'll get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He's going to guide us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Okay, look, just as an asterisk, I'm not asking you because the Bible is such a great authoritarian book. It's not that at all. In my view, if you want to know where this, what you call the sanctity of property, where does the sanctity of property comes from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It comes from the Ten Commandments. It comes from Moses saying, I haven't taken anything from anyone. It comes from Samuel saying, I haven't taken anything from anyone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's the condemnation of Ahab, of the unjust kings who steal the property of their subjects. So I'm not, so property and freedom, I think there's great basis for it in the Bible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But right now, I'm focusing on this other question, which is what happens when everyone does what's right in his own eyes? That's the book of judges and that's this civil war, moral corruption, theft, idolatry, murder, rape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, that's what happens when everyone does whatever is right in his own eyes. Well, no, that's what it says in the text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm not. Okay. So when I look at, you're right, there are things that I think are objectively true. I think it's really hard to get people to agree to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Almost impossible. But when I look at a country which is approaching one birth per woman, in other words, half of the minimum necessary for replacement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: you can say whatever you want, whatever you want about immigration, we can have that discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But the point is that when your values are such that you're not even capable of doing the most basic techniques that human beings need in order to be able to propagate themselves and their values and the way they see things, then I look, you're finished.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can't say that. So if I implied that Japan is an ideal society, I take that back. But let's think about Japan for a minute. I just think we're in trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I agree with you. Give me a second. Hold your laugh. It's his show, man. We enter into his hierarchy. That's it. We should talk about Hayoki.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Just to clarify, how do you explain the situation in Japan? Is it the decrease in value in family? Just expand on that. How do you explain that situation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You're saying that society is in trouble in a certain way. Can you kind of describe the nature of that trouble?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm saying that when the individual is part of a social group, this can be a family, a congregation, a community, a tribe, a nation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: When the individual feels that the things that are happening to the society are things that are happening to him or to her.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I want to emphasize, this is not the standard view of collectivism that Mussolini will say the glory of the individual is in totally immersing himself in the organic whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's not what I'm saying. I'm saying that human beings have and are both. They enter into a society to which they are loyal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And they compete with one another in the terms that that society allows competition, but also sometimes by bending the rules and by shaping them and by changing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What you see in many societies, certainly throughout the liberal West, but also in countries that have been affected by the liberal West, by industrialization and ideas of individualism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: what you see is a collapse of a willingness of the individual to look at what is needed by the whole and to make choices that are, as your own would call them, selfish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because the purpose of them is self-expression, competition, self-assertion, moving up in the hierarchy, achieving honor or wealth in order to do those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But when you stop being able to look at the framework of a particular society and identify with it, you cease to understand what it is that you need to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Not every single person, but I'm talking about society-wide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So there are few individuals who are just going to have a fantastic time and live the kind of life that you're on is describing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the great majority, they stop being willing to take risks. They stop being willing to get married. They stop being willing to have children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They stop being willing to start companies. They stop being willing to put themselves out to do great things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because the guide rails that told them what kinds of things and the social feedback that honored them when they did things like getting married and having children, they've been crushed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what have they been crushed by? They've been crushed by the false view that if you tell the individual, be free, make all your own decisions, that they will then be free and make all their own decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They don't. They just stop. They stop being human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's powerful. So do you want to respond to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes. So I don't think anybody should have children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If the goal, there's a good tweet clip that you can make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't think anybody should have children for the goal of perpetuating their nation or expanding their society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think they'd make horrible parents if that was the goal, the purpose of doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think people should have children because they want to embrace that challenge, that beauty, that experience, that amazing, very, very hard, very, very difficult experience in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's about being able to project the long term, but also being able to enjoy and love the creation of another human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That process of creation, it is a beautiful, self-interested thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And by the way, not everybody should have children. I think way too many people have children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's some awful parents out there that I wish would stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, there are. Life is precious and life of suffering is sad. It's sad to see people suffer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And a lot of people are born into situations and born into parents that destroy the capacity to ever live a good life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that's a tragic and sad thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I don't measure the health of a society in how many children they're having or a health of a couple, whether they have children or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Those are individual choices. Some people make a choice not to have children, which is completely rational and consistent with their values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now, when you look at a society overall, I do think having children and not having children is a reflection of something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think it's a reflection of a certain optimism about the future. I think it's a reflection of thinking long-term versus short-term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think a short-term society doesn't have children. People don't have children there because children are long-term investment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They require real planning and real effort and real thinking about the long-term. But those are moral issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And again, we're confusing or mixing. When I say Japan, look how well Japan has done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't mean the specific Japanese people and how many kids they're having and what kind of life they're having in terms of these kind of particulars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But think about the alternatives Japan faces if you look around the options that they face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They tried empire. They tried nationalistic empire. It didn't turn out too well for them or anybody who they interacted with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They could have become North Korea. We know how that turned out. We know what that is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If you've been to Cambodia and seen the kind of poverty, and yes, maybe Cambodians have lots of children,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: but God, I'd rather be in Japan any day than have children in the kind of poverty and horrific circumstances they have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But in the context of the available regimes that were possible post-World War II for the Japanese to embrace,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the first one that generally led to prosperity, to freedom, to individuals pursuing values, not perfectly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: because they didn't implement the philosophical foundation, the moral foundation that I would like them to have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're still being impacted by Kantian, Hegelian, whatever philosophy that's out there in the West that's destroying the better parts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you give people freedom. Now, what do they do with it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If they have a bad philosophy, they're going to do bad things with that freedom. You tell people to do whatever they choose to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But if they have bad ideas, they will choose to do bad things.
