metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I have to do the thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It won't be mine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It'll be Ayn Rand's, but it won't be mine unless I've done the thinking to integrate it into my soul, into my consciousness, into my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But it's still true that I have to think for myself, not on a desert island.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I now regret ever using a desert island in the book as an example because...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We've achieved something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There is progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're moving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because clearly it was misunderstood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I didn't make myself clear enough in the book in terms of what I meant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But, you know, I do not advocate for thinking alone in a dark room, not engaging with reality, not studying history, not knowing about the world, or on a desert island, not interacting with other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you're a collectivist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, I'm a trader.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I enjoy what we're doing right now because you're challenging me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You make me a better thinker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, the fact that a lot of people are going to watch this plays into it as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I would probably enjoy engaging with you in conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's not even recording, so...

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah, there you go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I would enjoy engaging with you, with your own conversation, even if it wasn't being recorded and even if it was because, you know, that kind of conversation makes me better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's some people who I wouldn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There's some people who make it worse, right, that you want to walk away from the conversation because they're harmful to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this is where choice comes in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I want to be able to choose who I engage with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't always have that choice because as a public intellectual, you go in front of audiences, you don't always choose who it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But you want to choose who you engage with and who you don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You want to choose the forum in which you engage and how you engage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the standard for me is reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There is no other standard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you asked a deep question to start off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Why reason?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because that's where the values come from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's the only tool we have to discover truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes, you know, reason is something that it doesn't guarantee truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It doesn't guarantee the world is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's fallible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But it's all we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's the tool in which we evaluate the world around us and we come to conclusions about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: There just isn't other tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Emotions are not tools of cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Consciousness is a tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Emotion, like love, all of these things are ways to experience the world, to say that reason is the best tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But there's a difference between experiencing the world and evaluating the world in terms of what is truth or what is not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: As a scientist, I appreciate the value of reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And emotions and love are consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're not primary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Emotions are consequences of conclusions you've come to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Your emotions will change very quickly, relatively speaking, when your evaluations of a situation will change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Different people can see exactly the same scene and have completely different emotions

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: because they're bringing different value systems and they're bringing different thoughts to the process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Maybe love is primary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But let me ask.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Love is the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can fall out of love with somebody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Because you learn something new because you've discovered something new about the person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Now you don't love them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's the wrong podcast to bring up love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We'll talk forever about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, you wrote the book, The Virtue of Nationalism, contrasting nation states with empires and with global governance like United Nations and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, you argue that nationalism uniquely provides the, quote, the collective right of a free people to rule themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, continuing our conversation, why is this particular collection of humans, we call a nation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: a uniquely powerful way to preserve the freedom of a people, to have people rule themselves?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Before I say anything on the subject, I should emphasize that I'm not a rationalist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm an empiricist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I'm offering what I think is a valid observation of human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't have some kind of deductive framework for proving that the nation is the best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And empirically, we know something about the way systems of national states work and about the way empires work and the way tribal societies work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What we don't know is, you know, is it possible to invent something else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I mean, there's a lot of things we don't know here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, with the caveat that I'm making an empirical observation, the basic argument is human beings form collectives naturally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: loyalty groups, and for most of human history and prehistory, as far as we know, human beings lived in tribal societies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Tribal societies are societies in which there's constant friction and constant warfare among very small groups, among families and clans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And we reach a turning point in human history with the invention of large-scale agriculture, which allows the creation of vast wealth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It allows the establishment of standing armies instead of militias.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, Sargon of Akkad says, I can pay 5,000 men to do nothing other than to drill in the arts of war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and then I'm going to send them out to conquer the neighboring city-states, and there you have empire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The Bible, which is the source of our image, our conception of a world of independent nations that are not constantly trying to conquer one another,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: the source of that is the Bible, and the biblical world is one in which Israel and various other small nations

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: are trying to fight for their independence against world empires, against empires Babylonian, Assyrian, Persian, Egyptian, which aspire to rule the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: My claim is fundamentally twofold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's moral that whenever you conquer a foreign nation, you're murdering and you're stealing, you're destroying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: As your own would say, you're using force to cause people to submit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So there is something in the prophets that rebels against this ongoing atrocity and carnage of trying to take over the whole world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And there's a prudential practical argument, which is that the world is governed best when there are multiple nations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: when they're free to experiment and chart their own courses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That means they have their own route to God, they have their own moralities, they have their own forms of economy and government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And what tends to happen in history is that when something is successful, when something looks like when people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: a different nation looks at and say, well, those people are flourishing, they're succeeding, then it's imitated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And in the way that the Dutch invented the stock market and the English said, look, that makes them powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So we'll adopt it. So there's endless examples of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So that's the argument for it. The argument is since we don't know a priori deductively from self-evident principles, what is best,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: it's best to have a world in which people are trying different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So a quick question, because the word nationalism sometimes is presented in negative light in connection to the nationalism of Nazi Germany, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So you're looking empirically at a world of nations that respect each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I use the word nationalism the way that I inherited it in my tradition, which is it's a principled standpoint that says that the world is governed best

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: when many nations are able to be independent and chart their own course. That's nationalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: As far as the Nazis, Hitler is an imperialist. He hated nation states. His whole theory, if you pick up, I don't recommend doing this, but if you do-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Actually reading it right now, Mein Kampf.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Right. If you do read Mein Kampf, then you'll see that he says explicitly that the goal is for Germany to be the lord of the earth and mistress of the globe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he detests the idea of the independent nation state because he sees it as weak and a feat. He might as well have said it's Jewish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So let me ask from the individual perspective for nationalism, what do you make of the value of the love of country?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The reason I connect that, so I personally, what would you say, a patriot? I love the love of country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Or I am susceptible, or how should I, in a Randian way, I enjoy, I in a-

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Love is good. Love is a good word. Don't come from away from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, I love a lot of things, but I'm saying this particular love is a little bit contentious, which is loving your country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's an interesting love that some people are a little uncomfortable with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Even when, especially when that love, you know, I grew up in the Soviet Union to say, you know, you just love the country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It represents a certain thing to you. And it's not, you don't think like philosophically, like I was marching around with like marks under my arm or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's just loving community at the level of nation. It's very interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't know if that's an artifact of the past that we're going to have to strip away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't know if I was just raised in that kind of community, but I appreciate that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I guess the thing I'm torn about is that love of country that I have in my heart, that I now love America and I consider myself an American.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That would have easily, if I was born earlier, been used by Stalin and I would have proudly died on the battlefield.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I would have proudly died if I was in Nazi Germany as a German and I would probably die as an American.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Are you sure about these things? Yes. That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: No, I think about this a lot. It's interesting to run a radical counterfactual and be sure of the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm not sure. I mean, but I think about this a lot because obviously I'm really interested in history and I put my, this is the way I think about most situations is I empathize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I really try to do hard work of placing myself in that moment and thinking through it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I'm just OK. I just know myself psychologically. What? What I'm susceptible to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's a negative way to phrase it, but what I would love doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so I'm just saying my question is, is the love of nation a useful or a powerful moral, sort of from a moral philosophy perspective, a good thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think it is a good thing. But before we ask whether it's a good thing, I think it's worth asking whether there's any way to live without it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The idea of national independence of a world or a continent which politically is governed by multiple independent national states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is a political theory. Somebody came up with that, you know, in the Bible or elsewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Someone came up with this idea and sold it and a lot of people like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But the nation is not an invention. Every place in human history that we have any record of, there are nations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so the fact of people creating families, families creating an alliance of clans, clans creating alliances of tribes, tribes creating alliances of

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and an alliance that becomes the nation. We see that everywhere in human history, everywhere we look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the love of a group of tribes that have come together in order to fight opponents that are trying to destroy your way of life and, you know, steal your land and harm your women and children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The love of the leadership that brings it together here. This is, you know, a George Washington type figure or an Alfred the Great type figure or Saul, the biblical Saul.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Somebody who has the wisdom, the daring to unite the tribes, overcome their, you know, their internal mutual hatreds and grievances and rally them around a set of ideas, a language, a tradition, an identity, as people say today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That love is eradicable from human beings. Maybe we'll have Brave New World, people will take drugs in order to get rid of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The problem is that could be leveraged by authoritarian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yes, but that's true of everything. It's like saying, you know, you can have children and you can teach them to be evil. You can make a lot of money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You can use it for evil. You can have a gun for self-defense, but you can use it for evil. Come on. We did. That's that's human. That's being human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You guys are making love this primary, which I don't think it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: How dare you, your honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I know there are lots of people in the world that they who don't love their nation because the nation is not worth loving. That is love is conditional. It's not unconditional. Love is conditioned on the value that's presented to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: You know, so I lived through this experience in my own life. I was I grew up in Israel at a time of everything was geared towards patriotism and the state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Breeze up until now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What gives you hope about the future?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So we've been describing reasons to maybe not have hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What gives you hope?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: When you look at the world, what gives you hope that in 200 years and 300 years and 500 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: like the founders look into the future, that human civilization will be all right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And more than that, it would flourish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Two things for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: One is history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So in the very long run, good ideas win out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think in the very long run, you can go through adult ages, but you come out of adult ages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The good and the just does win in the end, even if it is bloody and difficult and hard to get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So while I am quite pessimistic, unfortunately, about the short run, I'm ultimately optimistic that in the long run, good ideas win and they're justified.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think the fundamental behind that is that I'm fundamentally positive about human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think human beings can think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're capable of reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're capable of figuring out the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They're capable of learning from experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They don't always do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's an achievement to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But over time, they do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And if you create the right circumstances, they will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And when things get bad enough, they look for a way out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They look at maybe at history, if the history is available to them, maybe at just learning from what's around them to find better ways of doing things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that reinforces itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But human beings are an amazing creature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're just amazing in our capacity to be creative and our capacity to think and our capacity to love and our capacity to change our environment, to fit our needs and to fit our requirements for survival

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: and to learn and to grow and to progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so again, long term, I think all that wins out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Short term, in any point in history, short term, right now, it doesn't look too good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What about you, Joran?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, as usual, I moved by what Joran says and I hear scripture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the source for Joran's hope is the Book of Exodus, which is the first place in human history where we are presented with the possibility that an enslaved people that's being persecuted and murdered and living under the worst possible regime

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: can free itself and have a shot at a life of independence and worth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's another inherited Jewish ideal in the tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The way that we express this is by saying that there is a God who judges.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The Israelites in Egypt were enslaved for hundreds of years, according to the Exodus story, hundreds of years before God wakes up and hears them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he doesn't do anything until Moses kills the oppressor and goes out into the desert.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So I think it's pretty realistic that there is a God that God judges and acts, but probably often not for a very, very long time and not until there's a human being who gets up and says enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I know that today people don't want to read the Bible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They don't like reading the Bible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But I always hear in my ear this cry of the prophet Jeremiah, who saw his nation destroyed and these people exiled.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he says in God's name, he says, he's not my word like fire, like the hammer that shatters rock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: A patishim and a petzelah, my word is like fire, like the hammer that shatters rock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And this is actually, this is the traditional way of saying something like what your honor is saying, that it may take a long, long time, but there is a truth and it has its own strength.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it will in the end shatter the things that are opposing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's our traditional hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We grow up like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And so I do have hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I see the trends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: The trends are terrible right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it's frightening and it's hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But we are terrible at seeing the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And it is very possible that an unexpected turn of events is going to appear maybe soon, maybe much later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And the possibility of a redemption is there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Let me ask, given that long arc of history, given that you do study the Bible, what is the meaning of this whole thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What's the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Wow, that's beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think that the meaning of life is in part what your own touches on when he says that the productive work, labor, creativity is at the heart of what it is to be human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I just think that there are some more arenas, and maybe we even agree with a lot of them, and on a lot of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: To be human is to inherit a world which is imperfect, terribly imperfect, imperfect in many ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And God created it that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: He created a world which is terribly lacking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And he created us with the ability to stand up and to say, I can change the direction of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I can do something to change the direction of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I can take the time and the abilities that are given to me to be a partner with God in creating the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's not going to stay the way it was before me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It'll be something different, maybe a little bit, maybe a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But that is the heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is the key.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That is the meaningful life, is to be a partner with God in creating the world so that it is moving that much more in the right direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: rather than the way we found it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, a nudge, even if a little bit, the direction of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Well, you've actually been talking and you program about life quite a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So, let me ask the same question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I never tire you asking this question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What do you think is the meaning of this whole thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I don't believe in God, so God doesn't play a role in my view of the meaning of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think the meaning of life is to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I like to say to live with a capital L. It's to embrace it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I agree with you all in a sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're born into a world and as human beings, one of the things that makes us very different than other animals is our capacity to change that world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can actually go out there and change the world around us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can change it materially through production and through the…

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can change it spiritually through changing the ideas of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can change the direction to which humanity works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We can create a little universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I think part of the joy of creating a family is to create a little universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're creating a little world around us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: That's part of the joy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And there is joy in family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: We're not talking about difficulty and hard work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Part of the idea of getting married is to create a little world in which you and your spouse are creating something that didn't exist before and building something, building a universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: But it's really to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: One of the things that I see and that saddens me is wasted lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: It's people who just cruise through life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They get born in a particular place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They never challenge it. They never question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They just live, die, and nothing really happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Nothing really changed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They didn't produce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: They didn't make anything of their life and produce here again in the largest sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So to me, it's in every aspect of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: As you know, because you've listened to my show, I love art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I love aesthetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I love the experience of great art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I love relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I love producing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I like business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: I like that aspect of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And I think people are shallow in so many parts of their lives, which saddens me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: If you had 8 billion people on this planet, even if it never grew, even if we just stayed at 8 billion, but the 8 billion all lived fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What an amazing place this would be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: What an amazing experience we would have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: So to me, that is the meaning is just make the most of it. You have a short period of time on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And that's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: This is it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And live it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Experience it fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And challenge yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: And push yourself.

body.input: And let me just say something about optimism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: One source of hope for me in the world in which we live right now is that there are people who do that, at least in certain realms of their lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nationalism Debate: Yaron Brook and Yoram Hazony | Lex Fridman Podcast #256

body.input: Let me ask the big question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: did the human brain evolve to think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: That's essentially the question that you address in the essay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: Can you speak to it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: Sure, the big caveat here is that we don't really know

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: why brains evolved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: The big why questions are called teleological questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: and in general, scientists should avoid those questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: because we don't know the why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: However, for a very long time, the assumption was

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: that evolution worked in a progressive upward scale

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: that you start off with simple organisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: and those organisms get more complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: and more complex and more complex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: Now, obviously that's true in some really general way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: that life started off as single cell organisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: and things got more complex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: but the idea that brains evolved in some upward trajectory

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: from simple brains in simple animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: to complex brains in complex animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: is called a phylogenetic scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: And that phylogenetic scale is embedded

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: in a lot of evolutionary thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: including Darwin's actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: And it's been seriously challenged, I would say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: by modern evolutionary biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: And so thinking is something that,

body.input: as a great human achievement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Love, Evolution, and the Human Brain | Lex Fridman Podcast #140

body.input: And so the idea that the most common evolutionary story

body.input: is that brains evolved in like sedimentary rock

body.input: And now, here's my conversation with Neil Stevenson.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: You write both historical fiction, like World War II in Cryptonomicon, and science fiction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: So let me ask, does history repeat itself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: I'm afraid it repeats itself a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: So I think human nature kind of is what it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: And so we tend to see similar behavior patterns emerging again and again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: And so it's kind of the exception rather than the rule when something new happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: What role does technology play in the suppression or in revealing human nature?

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: Well, the standards of living, life expectancy, all that have gotten incredibly better within

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: the last, particularly the last 100 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: I mean, just antibiotics, modern vaccines, electrification, the internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: These are all improvements in most people's standard of living and health and longevity

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: that exceed anything that was seen before in human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: So people are living longer, they're generally healthier, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: But again, we still see a lot of the same behavior patterns, some of which are not very

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: attractive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: you have less and less constraints on resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: So we get to maybe emphasize the better angels of our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240

body.input: And in so doing, does that not potentially fundamentally alter the experience that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Neal Stephenson: Sci-Fi, Space, Aliens, AI, VR & the Future of Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #240
