body.input: And then at the end, play at the dance to save his parents with Johnny B. Goode. Pretty awesome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, the guitar is so much more than a musical instrument. It feels like... It's like the... In the 20th century, it's like the car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It defines so much of Hollywood, so much of a generation of what it means to be... I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What it means to be a man, what it means to be a human in America. It's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's emblematic to me of a certain type of music. I made a documentary years ago called It Might Get Loud with Jimmy Page, The Edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I highly recommend that everybody watch that documentary. It's an incredible celebration of the guitar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, it says Jimmy Page, Jack White from White Stripes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: The Edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And The Edge from U2. Okay, all right. Well, now you have to tell the story of that one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Because how the heck did that all come together? Because it's so fascinating. Such different musicians all coming together, talking about their story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: talking about how they approach the music, and also playing together a little bit in this casual kind of setting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Well, look, one day I came downstairs and the Rolling Stone magazine is sitting there and it was the 50th... It was the 50 top guitarists of all time, their list.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And then I had some other financial report with video games and the top video game at the time was Guitar Hero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And then there was a third thing, I can't recall it, but I just... And I said to myself, what is it about the guitar that is so central to the rock and roll,

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: whatever you want to call it, why is that the symbol? And I said to myself, I want to ask Jimmy Page why he picked up the guitar, because he's Jimmy Page, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And so I called a friend of mine, Davis Guggenheim, who had directed Inconvenient Truth, and I think still is, but at the time was the biggest documentary ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And I called Davis and I said, look, I have this idea, I want to make this movie about the guitar, about different eras and styles and whatever, but I've never made a documentary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I don't know how to do that. And so I was just looking for advice. And thankfully, because he's one of the best documentarians ever, Davis is like, you know what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I can't get this out of my head. I'll direct it, which was amazing. And we wrote three names down that represented different eras and different styles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Rarely do you go three for three, but it was those three guys. And it was just such an incredible experience to sit there and get to know Jimmy Page.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And he was like Gandalf, man. He was like always Jimmy Page.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, yeah. That was so cool to see him. Gandalf was good. There's like a wisdom, there's a calmness to him compared to like the restlessness of Jack White.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I mean, that combination was just fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It was one of the coolest experiences ever. And one of the things, there was a moment where Jimmy, he was going through his guitar case and he had the double neck from stairway to heaven and he handed it to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And I was like, mm-hmm. I mean, it's like somebody handing you X caliber or something. Amazing experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And The Edge, one of the kindest human beings you'll ever meet in your life. Just an amazing person. And I think you hit it right in the head with Jack is he's got that energy and constantly pushing himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But it's hard to believe it's been, I think, 10 or 11 or maybe even 12 years since it came out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: After watching it, I realized how much it was needed. And I was almost surprised it didn't already exist. It was like, yeah, the guitar wasn't quite celebrated explicitly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: We almost didn't acknowledge it. How important it was culturally. It's kind of amazing. And the way it closed from the song, The Wait, it's called The Wait by the band.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's because they didn't want to go home. We were shooting on a Warner Brothers soundstage for three days when we called it The Summit where the three of them came together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And the two things I'll never forget is when Jimmy starts to play the riff from Whole Lotta Love, Edge and Jack ceased to be rock gods or whatever and had the same 15-year-old kid feeling that I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You could see in their face. And then at the end, they're like, hey, can we play? We just want to, we don't want to go. Can we just play something acoustically?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So we printed out the lyrics. That's what they wanted to play. And they just sat there and sat on those couches and just such a good way. And yeah, incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What's your guitar rig set up like? You have a few guitars. First, let's just put on the line. So what's better, Les Paul or Strat?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Well, I'm not going to get into what's better because I'm sure that'll start a flood of whatever. For me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm going to say it's Strat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: All right. Well, I'm a Les Paul. My main instrument is a Les Paul.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But I, okay, okay. Let me just put it on the table. I'm speaking as somebody who literally, I don't think I've ever actually strummed a chord on a Les Paul.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I've been, maybe I'm-

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So you're uninitiated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Exactly. So I don't speak from experience, but it's probably because of Hendrix. I'm so deeply influenced by Hendrix that I just kind of followed in his footsteps and clapped in and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: The amazing thing to me is if you look back at Leo Fender and what the Gibson guitar company and Les Paul did in the fifties, those are still the shapes and the perfect thing today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Right? The Strat and the Telecaster and the Les Paul. And it's, they got it right way back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I have my main guitar, you got to name your guitar. So my main guitar is named Hazel and it's a 59 Les Paul. And there's something magical in that year, like a Stradivarius.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And they're just, there's something different about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I play that and then I play it through sort of my main rigs, either a 59 Fender Twin or a 65 Marshall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And then when we're on the road now, because when you use older vintage stuff, you just got to be super careful with the tubes and everything. It has to be reliable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So very nicely, the guys from 2ROCK sent me some of their amps and they're really, because I don't use any new stuff, but the 2ROCK stuff is pretty great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So that's actually what I'm using.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It gets close to the sound that you like with the Marshall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah. Yeah. It's new and reliable. So that's what I'm using on the road right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Do people use emulation? Do they use software? Is it still?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: They do. I personally don't. I go, you know, I don't have many pedals. I use a Clon, an old, you know, vintage Clon straight into the amp and that's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Just as old school as possible. Is there other cool guitars you have that kind of stand out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I have a bunch of what they call Blackguard Telecasters from the 50s, which are pretty great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What are those? Blackguard Telecasters?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah. So it just, you know, it's in the 50s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Oh, they actually legit have a Blackguard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Blackguard. But they're incredible. So.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What's the color of the Telecaster itself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Most of them are yellow with black and then they got into different configurations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But there's something. I have a 51 Telecaster that I play in Open G and in songs with Open G that just, again, there's something, you know, and I'll take all the help I can get in terms of making it sound great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I'll try to find the magic ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What's your writing process like for the music and the lyrics? Is there, do you have to go to the mountains? Is there whiskey involved?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What do you have to do? Or do you just write a little bit whenever you have a moment of free time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm a boring guy because I don't drink. I don't, I just, I figure I can screw things up plenty on my own without adding anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's a good call.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But, you know, for me, it either starts with a riff, just something that I think is an interesting, you know, riff or tone that I can kind of sink my teeth into a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And a lot of times I'll write a title and love a title and then start to backfill.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Oh, cool. So the title is almost like an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah. Like this is where I want to be and then start kind of writing it out. And again, I just have to know, am I writing from a character's point of view?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Am I writing about someone or something, you know, is like the narrator and, you know, what is this person? Are they happy? Are they sad? Are they, where are they in life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I don't know if all that like great writers, I'm sure would say, why don't you just write? You don't need all that. But that's for me, that's my process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm not so sure about that. And I bet you quite a lot of writers have created a world in their mind before they even put the simplest of words down. So yeah, there's quite a lot to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What's your favorite song to play? Is there some favorite ones you go to? Both play and kind of, I'm sure you love singing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: No, no, no, no. I'm neither talented nor do I have the desire. And I think, you know, if you come see the show, you won't see a microphone anywhere near me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But do you, I mean, do you hear like when you're thinking about lyrics, do you hear the idea of the words?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: 100%. And especially what's great, you know, with Trey is I write for his voice. And then we have these amazing backup singers that are just, and I can hear all of it. I just can't do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And so I'd say to, of our stuff, there's a song called Half My Fault that I play in Open G that just, I love playing the song. I love that energy. And then there's, we have a new blues album coming out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And there's a song called Baby We're Through, and it just stays on the one. And for non-musicians, that means like in a lot of rock and roll and blues, it's what's called a one, four, five progression from your kind of root note.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And you would hear, if you're a non-musician, if you heard it, you'd be like, oh yeah, that's a lot of songs. And this song just stays on the same groove, like La Grange or Shake Your Hips or any of those songs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And it's just got this unbelievable energy and it's fun to play. But I have to keep the same rhythmic thing going for the whole song.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: With that simplicity, I mean, the personality of the song can really shine. I mean, Trey's, I mean, that guy, really cool. It just comes through. I mean, I guess you need that from a lead singer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You gotta have that. And my other guitar player, Johnny Bob, he's a phenomenal, I mean, like a legitimate guitar slinger. We probably split the leads 70-30. And he is just, there's times sometimes I look over at him and I'm like, I'm being a fan right now, because what you just laid down is pretty good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: From a lead perspective, what's the most fun thing to play? What kind of stuff do you like? Do you like slow? Do you like, I mean, if you feel like thrill is gone. So if you look at B.B. King, sometimes one note just bending the shit out of that. What do you call that? Vibrato?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah. If I'm going to play the lead, it's a certain kind of feel. Slow blues is probably my favorite to play or something that's got a little more of that Chuck Berry drive where you can be rhythmic in the lead. I can't, the shredding thing that those guys do is that's not my...

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I was actually always able to do that really well. Like you mentioned people that pick up fat, like maybe it's the classical piano training. I could play super fast on guitar, super technical. But to me, the hardest thing and my favorite thing is it's just, it's probably less to do with the guitar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: More living on life that's worth playing a guitar for. It's like a certain kind of emotion that you can put into the notes and that has to do with bending notes. Well, like bending notes is a whole other art form of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I worked surprisingly a long time on Comfortably Numb. So David Gilmore does a lot of bending and they're simple. They sound simple, but the dynamics of them to express like a buildup in the way it's held and there's often a vibrato at the top for a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's almost like a sigh and a sigh of relief and the buildup. That's an art form for him that's hard to get right. It's not just playing a note, playing a note, playing a note. It's in that dynamic movement of a note that so much can happen. That's where the blues just happens to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Look, I'm a huge Freddie King fan too. You listen to these guys and you sit there and they're like, man, you're playing in a small range on the neck. But it's like, I know the notes you're playing and I'm playing them too, but not like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Gilmore is certainly one of those guys that's incredible guitar player. In yet another chapter of an amazing life, you love football. You play football? Yes. What positions do you play? Wide receiver.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Wide receiver. Awesome. So maybe we can talk a little bit about your love of football and the fact that you are part owner of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Yeah. So, I mean, where do we start? We start at the beginning. Let's start at the end. Why the Steelers? What attracted you to the, first of all, I think, not to be controversial, but one of the best uniforms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: The best uniforms in football in terms of just like black and gold. Just. D-Cal only on one side. Yeah, it's great. Yeah, the helmet. Look, I've bled black and gold since I was a little boy. I grew up in upstate New York and the first football game I ever saw was the Steelers in the Super Bowl.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: As a really little kid and it just, I mean, Jack Lambert and Joe Green and Franco Harris and those guys were like came down from Olympia, Mount Olympus or something. And I just was enamored with the team. And because we only had three channels, the only time I'd get to see them is occasionally when they were the game of the week or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And I just loved to me what they stood for, the toughness and they played football, you know, the way that I thought was great. I was a huge Jack Lambert fan, our Hall of Fame linebacker who just intimidated everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So that was like the, that was the decade of the Steel Curtain. I mean, arguably one of the great sort of defensive of in football history and also one of the greatest football teams period of in football history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I've been a lifelong fan and was very fortunate to meet Mr. Rooney. The Rooney family started the team in 1933, got to know him and just was asked to be part of the ownership group. I think it was the end of 2007.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: First year as part of the group in 2008, we won the Super Bowl and it was like beyond surreal and just beyond surreal. And you know, it's amazing to be able to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I mean, the Rooney family is one of those most revered in sports for the way they conduct themselves. Mr. Rooney passed away I think five years ago now and we lost him, but was a champion, helped build the league.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I mean, put the league as we know it together. More importantly, was a civil rights champion who created what we now call the Rooney rule to make sure that we're being fair about giving minority coaches a chance to get hired.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And just, just as one of the most kind and amazing human beings I ever, ever met.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's incredible what sport does, like to bring out the best in people, to give people hope, to inspire people. There is something about football that has all the elements of a great sport.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's the teamwork. It's the sort of the combat aspect of it. It's like it's the purity of it. It's of like strength and power and speed and all the elements of like last minute close calls required to win the game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And where referee decisions, of course, that's essential for a sport can screw up the whole thing. Just got all of it together. I think just, I don't know, it gives the drama and the triumphs are just beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Like some of my favorite memories. I don't know if it's an accident or this is common with people is just with friends watching football and connecting over that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, well, it's look, it's an incredible game because there's nowhere to hide, right? You're out there on the field. It, you know, it's a great game that requires not only all those attributes that you said, but it's incredibly complex game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So if you don't know what you're looking at and you don't understand how complex defenses are trying to disguise what they're doing, offenses are trying to overcome that and you can set up one play the entire game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But a team that plays well together, right? Knows their plays inside and out, knows their assignments inside and out, can overcome and beat a more physically gifted team because of that, you know, work that, that aspect of working together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And one of the things that I always loved about sports is just you're out there. There's a set of rules and there's a scoreboard. So at the end of that game, it says, and you can make excuses about the refs or this happened or that happened, but you know, at the end of the day, did you go out and compete?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: When you went out and were a competitor, how did it work out? Right? And the simplicity of that and the purity of that is something that I always have been drawn to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: What about the business of sort of owning a team or putting together a team or trying to like build up a team that's going to be a great team? Like, what are some interesting aspects that people might not realize that you can carry over from all the other experience you have in business?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I think the hardest thing about professional sports right now, it's individuals getting paid money to play a sport, which is different than, it's certainly different than amateur.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And the decisions that are hard is when you get to know somebody who's a player on the team and either they're at the end of their career or you need to go in a different direction and that person who's done everything that you've asked, whatever the coaches have asked of that person, and you get close to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And when they have to be traded, released or whatever happens, it's, you know, that's sad. And being able to stand back and in some ways be dispassionate and not be a fan, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm on the Baseball Hall of Fame board and one of the guys that's on the board of me is Jerry Rynsdorf and I think it was Jerry who said, you know, if you act like a fan, you'll be sitting with them, which I thought was kind of funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Well, I got to push back on that a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: As a by way of a fan asking a dumb question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Okay, let me just give some examples. It's very common in sport. It's funny you said this example of like certain great players going to another team right at the end of their career.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And it always makes me sad. It almost makes me want to wish that you kind of retired right there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: From a perspective of just like, do you ever as a owner, but just in that space, think about like the Steelers in the full arc of human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So not like as a business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Okay, this question might be absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I don't have to think about it as a business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm a minority owner so I can think about it almost as a fan, but I'm sorry, go ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, that's what I mean. I suppose this is a dumb question to think of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Like of a business in that way, not just investment, but like, like legacy of like what footprint would you leave on this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That is one thing that I can say unequivocally and I only have the experience that I have. But one of the things that I'm so proud of about the way the Steelers conduct themselves is, and that's the Rooney family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's the legacy of the Rooney family is asking constantly about what's right for the league, what's right for the players.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You know, what's the right thing to do here? And that's something that I would hear Mr. Rooney say all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I think that legacy is important because ultimately the team belongs to that city, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Belongs to those fans and you know, the owners are the custodians of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I think, and when you realize what sports teams mean to the fans, the memories that it creates, the bonds that it creates, it's a, you know, it's a responsibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And I think that you do have to think beyond the, you know, certainly not just dollars and cents, but just sports is a very big deal in our society and it has to be, I think, held to a standard that's not just, well, were we profitable this year?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's, there are other businesses for that. It is certainly a business.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I don't mean to romanticize to the point that it's not, but to me it's more than that, or at least my experience has been that it's more than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's a source of meaning for millions of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And you see that most like during COVID, for example, when there's so much desperation, so many people losing their jobs, so many people having to deal with the uncertainty, what the future holds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: There's something about sports that just unites us that again, the tragedy and the triumphs of sport, of uniting, of gathering together with your friends, with family, shared experience of over like this, yeah, over just team, over rooting for your team, for your city.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And the access, again, as I alluded to, we didn't have anything when I was growing up, but I would pour through the box scores. I was a huge Yankee fan and Steeler fan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And feeling some ownership of that, right, that I could read the box score and relive what they did and occasionally see them on TV and feel like I was part of that celebration when they won and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's a very powerful thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You've been exceptionally successful in a bunch of avenues and a bunch of efforts. What advice would you give to a young person today? A high school student, a college undergraduate that's thinking about career, maybe advice, not about just career, but about how to live a life they can be proud of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: We talked earlier about intellectual honesty and to me, that's the first step of just saying to the best of your ability, who am I and what's important to me and what do I want to do and accomplish?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: If you can start with that and develop some sort of rules-based philosophical, here's what I'll do, what I won't do. And that way you can be flexible and pliable and you're going to need to be, but if you still have a compass that tells you, hey, at least I know this is the path I'm going to take, I think that's very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: The rules you're referring to, the principles, that's kind of like underlying integrity. So knowing what lines you don't cross on this path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's exactly right. Because if you have those absolutes, there are many decisions that come into focus very quickly, right? Because, hey, that's not for me. Or, hey, I'm willing to do whatever it takes to do X, Y, and Z.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And it has to do with the thing you were talking about. It's kind of interesting. You mentioned earlier in the conversation about slippery slope and that's how often it happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Like how the slipping into unethical behavior happens. It's a slippery slope of little adjustments. You put stuff off. And I've been fortunate to not have to encounter these moments very much in my life, but I still encounter them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: That's what integrity, I think, looks like. As the slippery slope is happening, those little things, without drama, without making a show of it, making a decision that stands behind your principles and just walking away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah. And besides the big ideas, I'm going to change the world. I'm going to innovate. I'm going to do all those other things. I also start, if I'm giving any advice, which we can debate whether or not I should be giving advice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But just in terms of, well, let me start with this. Are you a good friend? Can you be counted on? Do you do what you say you're going to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Are you accountable to what you sign up for and do you hold others accountable? What does all that look like? And then I think it's being as intellectually curious and well read as you can be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: We live in a world that is designed to distract you. And being able to sit with your thoughts or go on a walk and think deeply about something and not just surface area. You text me, I text you back, and we decide the fate of the world based on a couple of text messages or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You don't want to lose touch, I think, with being well read and understanding and standing on great thinkers' shoulders and learning from those works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And then I also think that there's resiliency and then there's grit. And I heard someone say one time that those are slightly different. I know that there are all kinds of challenges in life that are tragic, that are unfair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: There's no question that's the world we live in. But for me personally, to try as much as possible not to be in the victim mindset, because unfair things are going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And we all want to live in an idealistic, just world. That should be what we aspire to. I haven't seen that yet. I haven't experienced that yet. But yet you still have to function in that world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So I think that that resiliency thing is very important. And then putting yourself out there, because if you play scared and you're always afraid to fail, this is probably a dumb way to get to the end of the podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: But there are times, especially on Mount West, I love the big sky out in Montana, Idaho, places like that. And when you look up at night, it's almost like I've never seen anything like this before, because there's no light pollution, so to speak.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And sometimes when I look up the most daunting problems that I'm experiencing, I'm like, those things have been there for a billion years or whatever, and I'll be gone and it doesn't...

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: The most famous person on earth, 200 years ago? Eh. So it's pretty fleeting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And so make sure you have a good journey, and especially coming out of COVID, I think telling people that you care about them and maintaining and cultivating your friendships and relationships, and they're not just transactional.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And making sure that someday when you're laying there, you can say, yeah, I was a good family member. I was a good friend. I was someone that could be counted on. I think all those things go into the mix of however you want to take the journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: So when you look up to the stars, do you think about that quickly approaching end of yours? Do you think about your own mortality? Do you think about your death? Are you afraid of your death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm a huge fan of Stoicism. I read a lot of Stoicism. I think Ryan Holiday's done a great job of bringing some of that back into the forefront. It's just really thought provoking to me, and rings, a lot of it rings, just hits me and says, I think that's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And that Momento Mori thing, which is, hey, we're all going to die, so you should contemplate it. There's a finality to this thing. And so I think if you can rightly frame that between fretting about it every day and being afraid and being so laissez faire that you think you're going to live forever, it'll influence some of the decisions you make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It will influence the way you attack things and hopefully the way that you live your life. So yes, I wouldn't say I obsess over it, and I wouldn't say it's omnipresent, but because I read a lot of Stoicism and just I think it's right to pause and say, who knows, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: There's going to be an expiration date. And if it happened tomorrow, have I done the things I wanted to do? And am I the person I wanted to be? And I think it's important along the way to check those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Yeah, I tried to make sure that I actually visualized this, that I'm okay dying at the end of the day, at the end of each day. Like, if this is the last thing I do in my life is talking to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: Oh, good Lord.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: I'm happy. I know you're joking, but I'm happy I get to live the life I do. And I think, Memento Mori, I think the Stoics have it right. And you have it right in saying, meditate on death enough to remember that this ride ends pretty quickly to help you appreciate every day and the people you love, the people close to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: And the cool shit that you're doing in your life, the cool shit you're creating. And the fact that you, Mr. Thomas Tall, are playing with the motherfucking Rolling Stones tomorrow. You are the man in so many disciplines, so respected, so successful. It's truly an honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: You sit down and talk with me today. Thomas, thank you so much for showing up in Texas and for talking on this silly little podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

body.input: It's great, man. I'm a huge fan of the show and have had a great time hanging with you and really appreciate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Thomas Tull: From Batman Dark Knight Trilogy to AI and The Rolling Stones | Lex Fridman Podcast #259

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: that do their work so perfectly well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: That is impossible not to be fascinated with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: So what do you imagine when you think about a virus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: Do you imagine the individual,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: sort of these 100 nanometer particle things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: or do you imagine the whole pandemic, like society level,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: when you say the efficiency at which they do their work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: do you think of viruses as the millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: that occupy a human body or a living organism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: society level, like spreading as a pandemic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: or do you think of the individual little guy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: Yes, I think this is a unique concept

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: that allows you to move from microscale to the macroscale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: All right, so the virus itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: that it essentially has a limited number of functions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: it needs to do, necessary functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: And it essentially has enough information

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: just to do those functions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: as well as the ability to modify itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: So, it's a machine, it's an intelligent machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: So yeah, look, maybe on that point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: you're in danger of reducing the power of this thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: and to ensure its survival and its success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: So, do you see it as intelligent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: I think the intelligence of a virus is in its simplicity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: with so little material and information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

body.input: But also, I think it's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90

metadata.title: Podcast: Dmitry Korkin: Computational Biology of Coronavirus | Lex Fridman Podcast #90
