body.input: so now they completely ignore the accept cookies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: This is very difficult to find that frictionless security.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: You mentioned Snowden.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: You've talked about looking through the NSA documents

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: he leaked and doing the hard work of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: What do you make of Edward Snowden?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: What have you learned from those documents?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: What do you think of him?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: In the long arc of history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: is Edward Snowden a hero or a villain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I think he's neither.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I have really complicated feelings about Edward Snowden.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: On the one hand, I'm a journalist at heart

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and more transparency is good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And I'm grateful for the conversations that we had

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: in the post Snowden era about the limits to surveillance

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and how critical privacy is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And when you have no transparency

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and you don't really know in that case

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: what our secret courts were doing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: how can you truly believe that our country

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: is taking our civil liberties seriously?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: So on the one hand, I'm grateful

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: that he cracked open these debates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: On the other hand, when I walked into the storage closet

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: of classified NSA secrets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I had just spent two years covering Chinese cyber espionage

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: almost every day and this sort of advancement

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: of Russian attacks that were just getting worse

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and worse and more destructive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And there were no limits to Chinese cyber espionage

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and Chinese surveillance of its own citizens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And there seemed to be no limit

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: to what Russia was willing to do in terms of cyber attacks

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and also in some cases, assassinating journalists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: So when I walked into that room,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: there was a part of me quite honestly that was relieved

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: to know that the NSA was as good as I hoped they were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And we weren't using that knowledge to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: as far as I know, assassinate journalists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: We weren't using our access to take out

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: pharmaceutical companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: For the most part, we were using it

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: for traditional espionage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: Now that set of documents also set me on the journey

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: of my book because to me, the American people's reaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: to the Snowden documents was a little bit misplaced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: They were upset about the phone call

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: metadata collection program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: Angela Merkel, I think rightfully was upset

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: that we were hacking her cell phone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: But in sort of the spy eats spy world hacking world leaders

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: cell phones is pretty much what most spy agencies do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And there wasn't a lot that I saw in those documents

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: that was beyond what I thought a spy agency does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And I think if there was another 9-11 tomorrow, God forbid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: we would all say, how did the NSA miss this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: Why weren't they spying on those terrorists?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: Why weren't they spying on those world leaders?

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And there's some of that too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: But I think that there was great damage done

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: to the US's reputation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I think we really lost our halo in terms of a protector

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: of civil liberties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And I think a lot of what was reported

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: was unfortunately reported in a vacuum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: That was my biggest gripe that we were always reporting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: The NSA has this program and here's what it does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And the NSA is in Angela Merkel's cell phone

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and the NSA can do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And no one was saying, and by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: China has been hacking into our pipelines

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and they've been making off

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: with all of our intellectual property.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And Russia has been hacking into our energy infrastructure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And they've been using the same methods to spy on track.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And in many cases kill their own journalists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And the Saudis have been doing this

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: to their own critics and dissidents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And so you can't talk about any of these countries

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: in isolation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: It is really like spy eats spy out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And so I just have complicated feelings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And the other thing is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: and I'm sorry, this is a little bit of a tangent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: but the amount of documents that we had,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: like thousands of documents, most of which were just crap,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: but had people's names on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: Part of me wishes that those documents had been released

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: in a much more targeted, limited way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: so they could cross match for counterintelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: who might be a likely Chinese spy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I talked to one critic, Ahmed Mansour, and he told me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: By that point, it turned out they'd already hacked

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: It troubles me deeply that MIT allowed somebody

body.input: I wonder how much malevolence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I don't know.

body.input: Let me ask you on a personal question.

body.input: of cyber warfare, cybersecurity.

body.input: Are you ever afraid for your own life,

body.input: I mean, I've had my moments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I describe in my book how when I was at that

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And then I've had moments where I think I went

body.input: And I was living by myself, I was single in San Francisco

body.input: and my cable box on my television started making

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: I mean, I'll never forget it.

body.input: or I could just do the best I can and live

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: in this new digital world we're living in.

body.input: And what does that look like for me?

body.input: For me, for the longest time, my crown jewels

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

body.input: And those were the lengths I was willing to go

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

metadata.title: Podcast: Nicole Perlroth: Cybersecurity and the Weapons of Cyberwar | Lex Fridman Podcast #266

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: If there's intelligent life out there in the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: do you think their mathematics is different than ours?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Jumping right in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think it's probably very different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: There's an obvious sense the notation is different, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think notation can guide what the math itself is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think it has everything to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: with the form of their existence, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Do you think they have basic arithmetic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: sorry, interrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Yeah, so I think they count, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think notions like one, two, three, the natural numbers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: that's extremely, well, natural.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: That's almost why we put that name to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: As soon as you can count,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: you have a notion of repetition, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Because you can count by two, two times or three times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And so you have this notion of repeating

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: the idea of counting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: which brings you addition and multiplication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think the way that we extend to the real numbers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: there's a little bit of choice in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: So there's this funny number system

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: called the surreal numbers

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: that it captures the idea of continuity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: It's a distinct mathematical object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: You could very well model the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: and motion of planets

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: with that as the back end of your math, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And you still have kind of the same interface

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: with the front end of what physical laws you're trying to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: or what physical phenomena

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: you're trying to describe with math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And I wonder if the little glimpses that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: of what choices you can make along the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: based on what different mathematicians

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: have brought to the table

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: is just scratching the surface

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: of what the different possibilities are

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: if you have a completely different mode of thought, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Or a mode of interacting with the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And you think notation is a key part of the journey

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: that we've taken through math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think that's the most salient part

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: that you'd notice at first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I think the mode of thought is gonna influence things

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: more than like the notation itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: But notation actually carries a lot of weight

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: when it comes to how we think about things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: more so than we usually give it credit for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I would be comfortable saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Do you have a favorite or least favorite piece of notation

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: in terms of its effectiveness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Yeah, yeah, well, so least favorite,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: one that I've been thinking a lot about

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: that will be a video I don't know when, but we'll see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: The number E.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: We write the function E to the X,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: this general exponential function,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: with a notation E to the X.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: That implies you should think about a particular number,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: this constant of nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: and you repeatedly multiply it by itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And then you say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: oh, what's E to the square root of two?

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: And you're like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: oh, well, we've extended the idea of repeated multiplication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: That's all nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: That's all nice and well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: But very famously, you have like E to the pi i,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: and you're like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: well, we're extending the idea of repeated multiplication

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: into the complex numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: Yeah, you can think about it that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: In reality, I think that it's just the wrong way

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: of notationally representing this function,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: the exponential function,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: which itself could be represented

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: a number of different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: You can think about it in terms of the problem it solves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: a certain very simple differential equation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: which often yields way more insight

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: than trying to twist the idea of repeated multiplication,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: take its arm and put it behind its back

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: and throw it on the desk and be like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: you will apply to complex numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: That's not, I don't think that's pedagogically helpful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: So the repeated multiplication

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: is actually missing the main point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: the power of E to the X.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: I mean, what it addresses is things where the rate

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: at which something changes depends on its own value,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: but more specifically, it depends on it linearly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: So for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: if you have like a population that's growing

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: and the rate at which it grows

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: depends on how many members of the population

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: are already there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: it looks like this nice exponential curve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: It makes sense to talk about repeated multiplication

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: because you say, how much is there after one year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Grant Sanderson: 3Blue1Brown and the Beauty of Mathematics | Lex Fridman Podcast #64

body.input: two years, three years, you're multiplying by something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Yeah, so in that paper,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: the concept I was trying to describe

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: is sort of an architecture for building

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: brain-inspired computing that leverages light

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: for communication in conjunction

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: with electronic circuits for computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: In that particular paper,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: a lot of the work we're doing right now

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in our project at NIST is focused on

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: superconducting electronics for computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: I'll go into why that is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but that might make a little more sense in context

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: if we first describe what that is in contrast to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: which is semiconducting electronics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So is it worth taking a couple minutes

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: to describe semiconducting electronics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: It might even be worthwhile to step back

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and talk about electricity and circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and how circuits work

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: before we talk about superconductivity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Right, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: How does a computer work, Jeff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Well, I won't go into everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that makes a computer work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but let's talk about the basic building blocks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: a transistor, and even more basic than that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: a semiconductor material, silicon, say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So in silicon, silicon is a semiconductor,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and what that means is at low temperature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: there are no free charges,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: no free electrons that can move around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So when you talk about electricity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you're talking about predominantly electrons

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: moving to establish electrical currents

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and they move under the influence of voltages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So you apply voltages, electrons move around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: those can be measured as currents,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and you can represent information in that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So semiconductors are special

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in the sense that they are really malleable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So if you have a semiconductor material,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you can change the number of free electrons

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that can move around by putting different elements,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: different atoms in lattice sites.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So what is a lattice site?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Well, a semiconductor is a crystal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: which means all the atoms that comprise the material

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: are at exact locations

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that are perfectly periodic in space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So if you started any one atom

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and you go along what are called the lattice vectors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you get to another atom and another atom and another atom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And for high quality devices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: it's important that that is a perfect crystal

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: with very few defects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: But you can intentionally replace a silicon atom

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: with say a phosphorus atom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and then you can change the number of free electrons

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that are in a region of space

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that has that excess of what are called dopants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So picture a device that has a left terminal

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and a right terminal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And if you apply a voltage between those two,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you can cause electrical current to flow between them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Now we add a third terminal up on top there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and depending on the voltage

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: between the left and right terminal and that third voltage,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you can change that current.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So what's commonly done in digital electronic circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: is to leave a fixed voltage from left to right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and then change that voltage

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that's applied at what's called the gate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: the gate of the transistor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So what you do is you make it to where

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: there's an excess of electrons on the left,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: excess of electrons on the right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and very few electrons in the middle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And you do this by changing the concentration

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: of different dopants in the lattice spatially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And then when you apply a voltage to that gate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you can either cause current to flow or turn it off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And so that's sort of your zero and one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: If you apply voltage, current can flow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that current is representing a digital one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And from that, from that basic element,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: you can build up all the complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: of digital electronic circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that have really had a profound influence on our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Now you're talking about electrons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Can you give a sense of what scale we're talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: when we're talking about in silicon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: being able to mass manufacture these kinds of gates?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Yeah, so scale in a number of different senses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Well, at the scale of the silicon lattice,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: the distance between two atoms there is half a nanometer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So people often like to compare these things

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: to the width of a human hair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: I think it's some six orders of magnitude smaller

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: than the width of a human hair, something on that order.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So remarkably small,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: we're talking about individual atoms here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And electrons are of that length scale

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: when they're in that environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: But there's another sense that scale matters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in digital electronics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: This is perhaps the more important sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: although they're related.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Scale refers to a number of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: It refers to the size of that transistor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So for example, I said you have a left contact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: a right contact, and some space between them

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: where the gate electrode sits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: That's called the channel width or the channel length.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And what has enabled what we think of as Moore's law

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: or the continued increased performance

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in silicon microelectronic circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: is the ability to make that size,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that feature size ever smaller, ever smaller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: At a really remarkable pace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: I mean, that feature size has decreased consistently

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: every couple of years since the 1960s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And that was what Moore predicted in the 1960s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: He thought it would continue for at least two more decades

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and it's been much longer than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And so that is why we've been able to fit ever more devices,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: ever more transistors, ever more computational power

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: on essentially the same size of chip.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So a user sits back and does essentially nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: You're running the same computer program,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but those devices are getting smaller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So they get faster, they get more energy efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And all of our computing performance

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: just continues to improve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And we don't have to think too hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: about what we're doing as say a software designer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: I absolutely don't mean to say that there's no innovation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in software or the user side of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Of course there is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but from the hardware perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: we just have been given this gift

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: of continued performance improvement through this scaling

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that is ever smaller feature sizes

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: with very similar say power consumption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: That power consumption has not continued to scale

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: in the most recent decades,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but nevertheless we had a really good run there for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: And now we're down to gates that are seven nanometers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: which is state of the art right now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: maybe global foundries is trying to push it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: even lower than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: I can't keep up with where the predictions are

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: that it's gonna end,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: but seven nanometer transistor

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: there's sort of a minimal amount that you have to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and it's KT log two.

body.input: And it's all somehow related to the second law

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: of thermodynamics and that the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: is an information process

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: and then we're living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So, okay, sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: Well, sorry for that tangent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: So that's the defining the distinction

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225

body.input: between computation and communication.

body.input: Let me say one more thing just to clarify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeffrey Shainline: Neuromorphic Computing and Optoelectronic Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #225
